articles.body: Diez campeones del mundo españoles figuran entre los principales aspirantes a los Beyond Developments Globe Soccer Awards 2026, cuyo resultado final se conocerá en Dubái el 28 de diciembre. La primera ronda de votación popular arranca este miércoles y se puede hacer en vote.globesoccer.com El talento español aparece en casi todas las categorías individuales. En la de Mejor Jugador, donde compiten 26 estrellas de todo el mundo, figuran Pau Cubarsí, Rodri, Lamine Yamal y Fabián Ruiz, que es además el único de la lista que ganó en 2026 tanto la Champions League como el Mundial. Pedri, además, opta al premio de Mejor Centrocampista, mientras que Cubarsí y Marc Cucurella, del Real Madrid, están entre los candidatos a Mejor Defensa. La portería es el terreno donde el dominio español resulta más evidente. Los tres guardametas campeones del mundo con la Selección, Unai Simón, David Raya y Joan García, están nominados a Mejor Portero, una lista en la que solo les acompaña el argentino Emiliano Martínez, que disputó la final del Mundial en Nueva Jersey. En el apartado femenino, Alexia Putellas figura entre las candidatas a Mejor Jugadora, categoría de la que queda fuera Aitana Bonmatí, ganadora el año pasado por tercera vez consecutiva, tras una temporada marcada por las lesiones con el Barcelona Femení. Los jóvenes españoles también tienen peso propio. Cubarsí y Carlos Espí, compiten en la categoría de Jugador Emergente, que reúne a catorce jóvenes figuras. En los banquillos, Luis de la Fuente, seleccionador campeón del mundo, y Luis Enrique, técnico del PSG, aparecen en la lista de diez candidatos a Mejor Entrenador, junto a Cesc Fàbregas, Arteta y Unai Emery, entre otros. La presencia española se extiende a los clubes. LALIGA cuenta con siete representantes en la lista de Mejor Jugador, el Barcelona Femení, que completó el cuádruple en 2026, está entre las seis nominadas a Mejor Club Femenino y el equipo masculino opta a Mejor Club Masculino. Por su parte, el Real Madrid encabeza la lista de 16 clubes del nuevo premio Fans’ Historic Club Award, que reconoce a los equipos con mayor tradición e historia. Los candidatos españoles tendrán que competir con un nutrido grupo de estrellas internacionales. Trece integrantes del PSG, bicampeón de Europa, están entre los aspirantes, entre ellos el defensor del título, Ousmane Dembélé, además de Achraf Hakimi, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia y Vitinha. También figuran Kylian Mbappé, Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice y Bukayo Saka. Lionel Messi, que ganó el premio en 2015, vuelve a estar en la carrera, y Cristiano Ronaldo defiende su título de Mejor Jugador de Oriente Medio, que ostenta desde 2023. La votación de 12 de las 14 categorías permanece abierta hasta el 30 de noviembre y en esta primera fase decide exclusivamente el público. En la segunda ronda, el voto de los aficionados se combinará con el del Jurado Globe Soccer, del que forman parte, entre otros, Marcello Lippi, Antonio Conte, Iker Casillas y Luis Figo. La gala servirá también de escenario para los galardones de LALIGA EA Sports de la temporada 2025-2026, ya confirmados. Lamine Yamal será reconocido como Jugador de la Temporada y Hansi Flick como Entrenador del Año. Carlos Espí, distinguido por su irrupción en el Levante UD y ahora en el Real Madrid, recibirá el premio al Mejor Sub-23. Arda Güler se llevará el de Gol de la Temporada por su disparo desde su propio campo ante el Elche en marzo, y Joan García recogerá el de Mejor Parada por su intervención ante el Espanyol en enero. La edición del año pasado reunió más de 30 millones de votos procedentes de más de 200 países y territorios. Esta 17.ª edición contará con 14 categorías, además de los habituales premios especiales y de carrera.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino at Man Utd: Incoming head coach calls for time to topple Man City ahead of Old Trafford arrival
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to restore Manchester United as the dominant force in the city, telling a former Manchester City player "you will see" when challenged over their supremacy; the Argentine insists he will need time to turn around United’s fortunes
articles.body:
The Argentine was speaking after taking charge of his final match as United States head coach, with a 2-0 victory over Haiti in Cincinnati completing an 8-0 aggregate win in their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final.

Pochettino will take charge of Manchester United for the first time against Liverpool on Sunday after being appointed to succeed Michael Carrick with long-term plans to re-establish the club's dominance.

Told by former Manchester City loanee DaMarcus Beasley that "Manchester is blue, it will always be blue" in the TNT Sports US studio after the game, Pochettino responded: "You will see. Give me time.

"The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it's adrenaline you want to feel.

"We need to add our common sense… we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United; the fan base is amazing."

Pochettino heads to Old Trafford having led the US to the last 16 at this year's World Cup on home soil.

"The mentality is to learn from everyone," Pochettino told reporters.

"You need to have an open mind because I think the players can teach us everyday, we are much better coaching staff now.

"Football is about attitude, and it's about the approach. It's about connection, feelings and communication."

articles.title: William Saliba or Ezri Konsa? Mikel Arteta has tough Arsenal selection dilemma when French defender returns to full fitness
articles.summary: Ezri Konsa has starred for Arsenal at centre-back following his £55m move from Aston Villa this summer, but William Saliba has now returned to take back his position in the Arsenal team; the Gunners have important games against Man City, Real Madrid and Spurs after the break
articles.body:
William Saliba is coming back, which is a major boost for the Premier League champions, but to say Arsenal have missed him in recent weeks has been an understatement. Ezri Konsa has stepped up.

Not only has Konsa stepped in brilliantly for the injured Frenchman, but he has even proven to be just as good as Saliba was in Arsenal's title-winning season. Some areas of the data show Konsa has performed at higher levels.

But with Saliba now back in training and stepping up his fitness, Arteta has a task to balance the reintegration of one of his most important players, whilst keeping arguably their most in-form player happy.

And given the likes of Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Tottenham, Real Madrid and Manchester United face the Gunners before Christmas, these calls are important.

Konsa came to Arsenal with the reputation of being excellent at two key areas: accurate passing and duel-winning abilities. Since making the move from Villa to north London, he has continued that trend.

He ranks second in the Premier League this season for both passing accuracy and the percentage of ground duels won. These numbers make him one of the best defenders in the league this season in terms of an all-round game.

This form would normally make a player like Konsa undroppable at any level. The only issue is that one of the best centre-backs in the world is returning, who has been one of the centrepieces of the immense defensive unit Arteta has formed at the club.

The area that shows the importance of Saliba is the average height of Arsenal's defensive line. This season, without Saliba, the Gunners backline has dropped by at least one metre, no matter whether it is attacking or defending. It is a marginal shift, but this level has fine margins.

When Saliba broke into Arsenal's team in the 2022/23 season, Arsenal's defensive line was transformed. Their defensive line went higher by two metres compared to the previous season - partly due to the Frenchman's pace, with Saliba regularly described as a 'cheat code' in the way he can snuff out transitions and counter attacks with ease.

That higher line keeps opponents further away from their goal, leading to a better press and subsequently more Arsenal pressure and possession. Arteta regularly says one of the key aims for his team is "not allowing the opponent to breathe."

Konsa has done his fair share of sweeping up in the Arsenal high line this season. He has made three successful last-man tackles this season, with some of the highlights being result-defining challenges to deny the likes of Chelsea's Morgan Rogers and Nottingham Forest's Liam Delap as Arsenal protected one goal leads to claim victory.

But on that note, the centre-back partnership of Konsa-Gabriel has made more last-man tackles between them this season (seven), than Saliba-Gabriel needed in the whole of last season (five). Opponents are not just breathing a little, they are threatening in open spaces a bit more.

In a system where Arsenal pride themselves on giving next to nothing away in terms of attacking chances to their opposition, there is value in bringing back the 'cheat code'.

One scenario where Konsa and Saliba could play together is by moving the England international out to right-back, where he has played before in his career.

That would also suit Arteta's full-back plans - with the Arsenal manager almost exclusively playing natural full-backs in his full-back roles in recent years. Jurrien Timber, Ben White, Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie were all centre-backs by trade before moving to north London and being retrained as wider options.

However, the last couple of years has seen Konsa specialise centrally - to the point where he hasn't played a Premier League match at right-back for nearly two years.

His last league start as a full-back came in December 2024 when playing for Aston Villa, with his last 5,813 league minutes - the equivalent of nearly 65 games - coming as a centre-back. "Ezri, yeah, he can play as a full-back," said Arteta earlier this month. "I think his main position is as a centre-back."

And of course, Konsa and Saliba could play at centre-back together, giving Gabriel a bit of a rest when needed. It would mean moving one to a left centre-back role - and taking a left-footed centre-back out of the team, but the Arsenal manager is confident in that.

"He can play right or left," said Arteta of Konsa. "Willy has done the same with the national team and here at Arsenal. That's going to be something really positive for the team."

And while this could be a headache of Arteta, this has emerged as a positive problem. Arsenal have felt the impact of an injury to Saliba and Gabriel in the past - it has sometimes cost them Premier League and Champions League titles in recent years.

Now they're in a better place, but Arteta still has to get these big calls right. The Arsenal manager has sometimes made questionable selection calls this season in terms of the profiles he has in his team.

In the 3-0 loss at Brighton, he gave Bruno Guimaraes a first start in midfield when perhaps the more press-resistant Myles Lewis-Skelly was a better option against the high-intensity Seagulls in the press.

And in the recent win over Hull, Arteta went for Kai Havertz up front when the game was screaming out for Viktor Gyokeres' bullish nature against the three Tigers centre-backs.

Now Arteta has the a similar dilemma, only in defence.

articles.title: Lewis Hall is England's best left-back - because the Newcastle player started out as a midfielder in Chelsea's youth teams
articles.summary: Lewis Hall excelled for England in their win over Spain in Madrid and is belatedly establishing himself as first-choice left-back. With insight from the man who played him as a midfielder during his youth career at Chelsea, Adam Bate picks out a key reason for the player's rise...
articles.body:
The situation seemed dangerous for England but Hall looked so comfortable in a central role. His performance in the 3-2 win in Madrid highlighted his quality with and without the football. In the first half, he completed five dribbles. Five more than Lamine Yamal.

He deserved to be at the World Cup in the summer. Most would have picked the Newcastle player but, unfortunately for Hall, the England head coach Thomas Tuchel was not among that number. They went into the tournament with arguably only one specialist left-back.

Ironically, however, those who know Hall best might not put him in that category either. In fact, that little pirouette that so befuddled Spain's World Cup winners had been a feature of his game when he was a youngster at Chelsea. He was no left-back as a kid.

"A lot of the time I was playing a 3-4-2-1 formation with 10s," Ed Brand tells Sky Sports . "I would put him as a 10 quite a bit because he had always been a central midfield player. If I played a 4-2-3-1 formation then I would play him as one of the 6s or the 8s instead."

Brand worked with Hall as head coach of Chelsea's Under-18 side when the player was among the youngest in the side at just 16. "What a good kid he is." So impressed was Brand that shifting him out to the left flank was merely a way of keeping him in the side.

"There were players who were older than him. Good players," he explains. "In certain games, where I wanted to keep him in the team, he might have to play at left wing-back even though I knew at that point it was not his favourite position. He was a midfielder."

He recalls one particular game away to Tottenham when he played him as an out-and-out full-back. "I was going to him, 'Look, this is how I will fit you in.' I just wanted 11 footballers in every position because we wanted to make sure we got on the ball." The rest is history.

"He started to play there a little bit more, a little bit more, and it just went from there. Now he is seen in most football fans' eyes as a left back. Whereas I know that growing up, he has always been an attacking player with the ability to get goals and run beyond."

Brand points to the key role of Andy Myers in developing Hall as a left-back at under-21 level. His game evolved. "He was excellent when he was a 10. But people adapt and see your football differently." And Hall's schooling in midfield still helps him.

"He is so comfortable at left-back because of where he is used to playing. When you are a player with his ability, used to playing in the centre of the pitch, seeing the game 360, you get moved to full-back, you look at it and think it is easy. He can see everything."

Brand talks of a player "showing all his attributes" and as seen against Spain he is hardly restricted to the touchline. "Full-backs in the modern game are so important with how they invert inside, they do a lot of stuff infield anyway. With his talent, he excels there."

Of course, the test against Lamine Yamal is off the ball as well as on it. Hall had mixed experiences against Barcelona's boy wonder earlier this year. Excellent in the home leg of Newcastle's Champions League tie, he was part of the side that conceded seven away.

At 22 years old, Hall is still learning himself. But he showed in Madrid that he is more than capable of doing the other side of the game. His attacking assets elevate him above most players in his position but he is certainly not a weak link defensively either.

"What is so impressive about Lew is how much he has improved upon his defensive side," agrees Brand. "You cannot play in the Premier League and not be able to defend to a certain level, He will continue to get better the more exposure he gets to that."

There will be more exposure, of that there is no doubt. His omission in the summer is ever more startling but the caps will keep coming now and an exciting club career is ahead of Hall too. A big test awaits in the Premier League against champions Arsenal on Saturday.

For Brand, there is pride at his development already and enthusiasm about his potential to improve even more. The former Chelsea midfielder has turned himself into England's outstanding left-back. "He has done brilliantly," concludes his former youth coach.

"In time, he will be one of those England internationals whose name will be one of the first on the sheet. I am biased but I already think there is a big enough case for it." After this latest showing in an England shirt, everyone, even Tuchel, is starting to agree.

articles.title: Nations League: Northern Ireland to take momentum into Euro 2028 qualifiers
articles.summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill says his Nations League promotion winners will plot their next 12 months after the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in December.
articles.body:
Speaking before his side ground out the required point against Hungary to seal top spot in Nations League Group B2, Northern Ireland's Trai Hume told reporters that automatic promotion had not been the most immediate aim coming into the campaign.

Two years ago, this side were a League C team, battling to return to the second tier from a group containing Belarus, Bulgaria and Luxembourg.

Fast forward 24 months and a League A place was secured on the final night of an unbeaten campaign that had looked a serious challenge. Prior the trip to Georgia in September, Northern Ireland had a record of played 10, lost eight and drawn two at this level.

Across six games in eight weeks, the side won three and drew three, conceding just once along the way. Justin Devenny's brilliant equaliser in Budapest on Tuesday secured the draw required to top the group and earn promotion to the top tier for the first time.

"It's a great feeling for us," said manager Michael O'Neill.

"In a way, we sort of set out when we came into this level of competition first of all to try and stay in it. Obviously to do that, you have to, you have to be in the top two positions.

"We knew that would help us potentially with the draw for Euro 2028, but to come away unbeaten, to to finish top and to give the performances we've given against some very good teams, it's very encouraging."

Northern Ireland draw with Hungary to seal Nations League promotion

Watch: Devenny the hero as NI earn promotion

Belief and bench help NI scale new heights

With such a young team on the international stage, there will always be more intangible markers of progress too.

It is perhaps easy to forget that not so long ago Pierce Charles' shot-stopping was being questioned as a weaker part of his game when compared to his range of passing.

Quite apart from a penalty save from Georgia's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to start the group, the Queens Park Rangers loanee made momentum-changing stops from Georges Mikautadze in Tbilisi and Danylo Sikan against Ukraine in Belfast last week.

All three of the Ruairi McConville-Tom Atcheson-Ciaron Brown defensive triumvirate have enhanced their reputations too, while, perhaps not yet in a first-choice XI, Patrick Kelly, Terry Devlin and Brodie Spencer feel increasingly trusted members of a deepening pool of players.

O'Neill may have only made nine changes to his starting teams across the six games, but it felt notable how often those coming in did not look out of place.

The bench then made a huge impact in the draw that sealed promotion with two players at opposing ends of the experience spectrum, Josh Magennis and Kieran Morrison, to the fore.

"We have a squad now where I think the younger players are coming in and making an impact straight away," said O'Neill, who still has the likes of Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard to come back into his squad.

"Which is a real positive, particularly if you look at the likes of Tom and Ruairi, but also Kieran Morrison and Ceadach [O'Neill] coming in and getting minutes early in their international careers.

"I just think that like the the squad is still very much still in development, we we still have areas where we still need to improve."

The next staging post for this Northern Ireland team is the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in Belfast on 6 December.

They will be among the second seeds thanks to their top-two Nations League finish and, depending on whether they land in a four or five-team group, could face qualifiers as early as March next year.

Not only did their Nations League performance win promotion to League A and a place with Europe's elite, it has also all but guaranteed a play-off for the Euros if the qualifying campaign does not go to plan.

"The great thing is we finish on a high and the players go back to their clubs now, they have to deal with a lot of football, they're all playing and demanding leagues," added O'Neill.

"Depending on the draw, we might come in in March and have friendly games which might be a nice thing for us to have.

"But we can just go in and see what the draw brings in December and then we can sort of plot the next 12 months."

After a string of impressive performances in the past three months, they will do so with serious momentum.

articles.title: El portero que 'fichó' Lunin: 500 minutos imbatido y en el radar de Mourinho
articles.standfirst: El 'boom Illia', portero ucraniano del Madrid C, es una realidad en Valdebebas, donde pidieron a su compatriota que le mandase un vídeo como parte de la estrategia para ficharlo
articles.summary: El 'boom Illia', portero ucraniano del Madrid C, es una realidad en Valdebebas, donde pidieron a su compatriota que le mandase un vídeo como parte de la estrategia para ficharlo
articles.body: En el año 2023 el mercado de cantera andaba revolucionado con un portero ucraniano de 16 años y 2,02 metros de altura que jugaba en el Rayo Majadahonda, que a su vez lo había incorporado del Novelda. Se trataba de Illia Voloshyn. En plena vorágine por su fichaje, un detalle ayudó a decantar la balanza en favor del Real Madrid: el joven portero recibió un vídeo de su compatriota Lunin. En estas operaciones todo cuenta y el Madrid acabó reclutando al prometedor guardameta de físico privilegiado en su búsqueda ya de un futuro sucesor de Courtois. Illia debutó en el Madrid el 3 de febrero de 2024 con el Juvenil C, en un derbi contra el Atlético en Valdebebas. Era el comienzo de su trayectoria en La Fábrica, que en los últimos meses está cogiendo una gran velocidad. El portero que 'fichó' Lunin es ahora, con 19 años, una de las sensaciones en Valdebebas. Debutó en pretemporada con el primer equipo en el amistoso ante el Schalke (lo hizo sustituyendo a Lunin), fue convocado para el Clásico tras la baja de última hora de Courtois y ahora mismo protagoniza una racha de 453 minutos imbatido con el Real Madrid C, equipo en el que está en plantilla y donde es 'titularísimo'. Illia lleva cinco partidos consecutivos imbatido (Tordesillas, Alcalá, Ávila, Valladolid Promesas y Sanse), que sumado al tiempo desde el último gol encajado ante el Guadalajara más todas las prolongaciones le acercan a los 500 minutos sin encajar. Illia ha jugado 10 partidos con el Madrid C en lo que va de temporada y ha dejado su portería a cero en siete ocasiones, encajando sólo cuatro goles. Unos registros eclipsados por el mal inicio de temporada del segundo filial blanco, al que le ha costado tomar el pulso a la competición. Desde el tercer filial lllia está proyectando su gigantesca figura hasta el primer equipo. Porque el meta ya está en el radar de Mourinho, tal y como demuestra su debut veraniego y el hecho de que se lo llevase de tercer portero al Clásico. Illia, representado por Unlimited Sports Management (USM), agencia de los representantes de Topuria, ha dado un salto de calidad esta temporada que lo ha posicionado entre los porteros de mayor proyección en el Real Madrid. Una circunstancia que está directamente relacionada con la figura de Mario Soria, el preparador de porteros del Madrid C, bajo cuyas órdenes el joven portero ha mejorado en muchos aspectos que van más allá de la portería, como la mentalidad, la autoexigencia y el hecho de sentirse importante bajo palos. Porque los primeros pasos de Illia por La Fábrica no fueron nada sencillos y durante mucho tiempo estuvo dando tumbos sin rumbo fijo. Hasta que la pasada temporada en el Juvenil A ya tuvo un gran protagonismo que lo acabó de catapultar. Una pubalgia de Javi Navarro a comienzo se año y el ascenso al Madrid C del que fue gran héroe de la Youth League dieron vía libre a Illia para asentarse a las órdenes de Álvaro López y dar un paso al frente que le valió su escalada al Madrid C para ser titular indiscutible. Ahora en los despachos de Valdebebas ya lo ven en el Castilla la próxima temporada, lo que supone estar un paso más cerca para hacer cumbre en el primer equipo.

articles.title: Güler renueva hasta 2032
articles.standfirst: El Real Madrid anuncia la ampliación del contrato del futbolista turco
articles.summary: El Real Madrid anuncia la ampliación del contrato del futbolista turco
articles.body: El Real Madrid ha anunciado este miércoles la ampliación de contrato de Arda Güler, que queda vinculado al club blanco hasta el 30 de junio de 2032. La entidad que preside Florentino Pérez premia así el crecimiento del futbolista otomano, que se ha convertido en apenas tres años en una de las piezas claves del equipo, sobre todo en la etapa de José Mourinho al frente de la plantilla madridista. Arda Güler llegó al Real Madrid en julio de 2023, con 18 años. En sus cuatro temporadas defendiendo la camiseta blanca, ha disputado 126 partidos, y ha ganado 5 títulos: 1 Champions League, 1 Mundial de Clubes, 1 Supercopa de Europa, 1 Liga y 1 Supercopa de España. Es internacional con Turquía, selección con la que ha jugado 38 partidos hasta el momento. Premiado el pasado mes de septiembre como Jugador Revelación de la Champions League 2025-2026, el crecimiento de Güler desde su llegada al club blanco ha sido exponencial. Aunque en un principio se vio frenado por las lesiones, poco a poco ha ido ganando peso en el equipo, hasta el punto de convertirse en uno de los referentes de la plantilla madridista en cuanto a talento. De hecho, y ya en esta temporada, Arda se ha convertido en una de las piezas clave del Real Madrid de Mourinho. Su consolidación en el once ha sido determinante en la reciente racha de los blancos, que ha permitido al equipo firmar un pleno de victorias en la Champions y depender de sí mismos en la Liga después de la victoria en el Camp Nou. El club premia con esta ampliación de contrato el gran rendimiento de Güler, al tiempo que lo blinda ante el interés de terceros, en especial de clubes de la Premier League. La renovación lleva aparejada una mejora salarial que coloca a Arda en el escalón medio-alto de la plantilla, a la altura de su importancia en el equipo. La de Güler es la primera renovación que el Madrid hace oficial desde la de Vinicius Junior, que se concretó el pasado verano. Pero no será la última. Como informó MARCA, el club blanco tiene ultimados acuerdos con otros pesos pesados de la plantilla, como Jude Bellingham o Thibaut Courtois, que se irán concretando de forma oficial en los próximos días o semanas. El turco celebró su renovación con un mensaje en redes sociales. "Historia que tú hiciste, historia por hacer. Cuando me puse por primera vez la camiseta del Real Madrid, sabía que entraba a formar parte de una historia inmensa. Hoy siento el mismo orgullo y la misma felicidad, pero con una responsabilidad aún mayor. Seguir los pasos de leyendas que han escrito su nombre en la historia del fútbol, en el club más grande del mundo, es un gran honor para mí. Mi sueño es vestir esta camiseta durante muchos años, ganar juntos nuevos títulos y, algún día, dejar mi propia huella en esta historia única. Quiero dar las gracias a todos los que han estado siempre a mi lado desde mi primer día: en especial a nuestro presidente, Florentino Pérez, a mi familia, a mis compañeros y a todo el staff y los entrenadores con los que he trabajado. Y el agradecimiento más especial, para los madridistas de todo el mundo, que siempre nos han dado un apoyo infinito. ¡A por muchos más días bonitos juntos! Estoy muy feliz de seguir siendo parte de este club. 2032".

articles.title: Ashley Williams set to join temporary Swansea City coaching staff
articles.summary: Ashley Williams is set to join a temporary Swansea City coaching team as the Championship club attempt to fill the void left by Vitor Matos.
articles.body:
Former captain Ashley Williams is set to join a temporary Swansea City coaching team as the Championship club attempt to fill the void left by the departure of Vitor Matos.

Williams, 42, is poised to work alongside fellow ex-Swans Kristian O'Leary and Leon Britton as part of interim coaching staff.

Head coach Matos is on the brink of completing a move to Strasbourg after just under a year in charge at Swansea.

Four members of Matos' coaching staff - Diogo Medeiros, Toze Mendes, Goncalo Ricca and head of goalkeeping Pedro Pereira – are also set to depart.

That leaves coaches O'Leary and Britton as the only remaining members of Matos' management team.

Swansea have therefore asked Williams to help out as they prepare for Saturday's home league game against West Bromwich Albion (15:00 GMT).

Latest Swansea City news, analysis and fan views

Listen to the latest Swansea City interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds

Swansea face a trip to Middlesbrough on Tuesday and then host the south Wales derby against Cardiff City on Sunday, 29 November, with no indication yet about when a new permanent management team will be in place.

Williams, who has worked as a pundit since retiring as a player in 2021, joined Craig Bellamy's Wales staff in September – alongside ex-Swansea boss Alan Sheehan – following the departures of James Rowberry and Piet Cremers.

The former Wales centre-back is regarded as one of the finest players in Swansea's history, having played more than 350 games for the club between 2008 and 2016.

He helped Swansea win promotion to the Premier League in 2011 - and go on to thrive for a spell at the highest level – while he captained the side in their 2013 League Cup final win over Bradford City.

The Swansea are sixth in the Championship, three points behind leaders Birmingham.

articles.title: Record crowds and legends - Bordeaux bid to return from French amateur sixth tier
articles.summary: Bordeaux fans thought things could not get any worse, then they were demoted to France's amateur sixth tier.
articles.body:
The latest stop on Zinedine Zidane's homecoming tour was an important one for the new France head coach. When Les Bleus took on Turkey in Bordeaux on Sunday night, the ex-midfielder was returning to the city in which he spent four formative years of his playing career, between 1992 and 1996.

"I became a man in Bordeaux," Zidane fondly recalled in the build-up. France edged triumphed 2-1 with an uninspiring display, but it did not dampen the mood of the 40,000 fans inside the Stade Atlantique.

While the 1998 World Cup winner was not necessarily in familiar surroundings (the out-of-town stadium was built for Euro 2016, 20 years after his departure for Juventus), locals made every effort to make him feel at home, holding up a commemorative tifo before kick-off and chanting Zizou's name throughout.

Just a few miles up the road earlier that afternoon, Zidane's former club were playing their fifth match of the season in the sixth-tier Regional 1, in a north-western suburb of the city.

Thousands of Bordeaux fans had made the short away outing to Saint-Medard-en-Jalles' 3000-seater ground to watch their team seal a fifth win in five this season.

Girondins de Bordeaux, the six-time French champions, who were once regulars in European cups, now find themselves facing amateur opposition on a weekly basis.

Since 2022, the club has plummeted from Ligue 1 to the sixth tier through a combination of on-pitch struggles, mismanagement at all levels, and sanctions due to their financial troubles.

Listen to the latest Football Daily podcast

The club was taken over in 2021 by Gerard Lopez, who was previously in charge of Formula 1's Lotus as well as another French side, Lille.

While Bordeaux were already hamstrung by debts at that point, the situation on and off the pitch worsened under the Spanish-Luxembourgish businessman as the men's first team finished rock bottom of Ligue 1 in his first season.

A couple of seasons in Ligue 2 followed, before the club was docked down to the fourth tier in 2024. In their first National 2 season, they notably signed Andy Carroll but ultimately missed out on promotion.

The following campaign saw a repeat of that near miss, and the club was expelled from national-level football altogether this summer over their finances.

With Bordeaux left on the brink and whittled down to just eight full-time employees (down from around 250 a few years beforehand), Lopez sold up to Park Bench, a group of mainly British USA-based investors who also own Scottish side Dunfermline as well as a minority stake in Spanish second tier side Cordoba.

The supporters turned out in their numbers for the first home match of the campaign, which had been delayed amid the uncertainty over whether the club could continue running, against Stade Montois.

More than 11,000 tickets sold, a record crowd for that level of French football.

"140 years of history, we won't be stopped," read one of the banners held up by the Ultramarines fan group, who also made it a point to thank the seven first-team players who had stayed despite the club's double relegation.

The team is centred around a core of players with Ligue 1 and Ligue 2 experience. Steve Shamal, who scored a hat-trick in that 4-1 victory over Stade Montois, previously turned out for the likes of Caen and Annecy in the second tier.

"We know we should be higher up, but that certainty can also be a trap," said Shamal after the game. "We shouldn't think that it's going to be easy.

"We need to respect our opponents if we're going to put in good performances."

As the sixth tier of French football is regionalised, only the league winner in the Nouvelle Aquitaine region's top flight will earn promotion.

Their on-pitch success so far this season comes as little surprise given the gulf in quality compared to the rest of the league. Over the summer, Bordeaux notably managed to hold on to Europa League-winning full-back Almamy Toure, while former Belgian youth international striker Baptiste Guillaume also joined.

Several former players have also looked to get involved in Bordeaux's revival.

Benoit Tremoulinas, the former French international who was a part of the title-winning squad in 2008-09, notably announced that at the age of 40 he would be lacing up his boots again seven years after injury forced him to retire.

Paul Baysse, the former centre-back, is an assistant to head coach Arnaud Cormier.

Perhaps the most significant endorsement the new owners could have hoped for was that of Alain Giresse, widely regarded as the club's greatest player. The Euro 1984 winner, who won three league titles while playing more than 500 times for the Marine et Blanc, was in attendance for the match against Stade Montois. He took the ceremonial kick-off before giving a full-time dressing room speech.

The new management unveiled their long-term plans for the club on Monday at Le Haillan, the city-owned training ground which includes a chateau that hosts the club's headquarters.

"We are humbled to have this responsibility," Park Bench investor Jeremy Green said.

"The club doesn't belong to Park Bench, it belongs to Bordeaux, it belongs to the 11,000 people who came to watch a Regional 1 game, to the players and to the community. We have a responsibility to rebuild this club.

"Our commitment to the community and to the players is that we will be fiscally responsible and patient.

"We're not a financial institution, we're a collection of individuals who bring with them business, sporting, analytical, and entrepreneurship skills."

Dominique Delport, the club's new president, revealed he knew Green and Twining through his wife, who studied at Oxford with them.

"We can learn from the club's golden years," the former journalist and advertising executive told BBC Sport, before adding that he would look to bring club legends to every league game.

While the club was sold for a symbolic euro, it did involve taking on long-standing debts which spanned transfer fees, stadium rent, and a compensation claim by former head coach Vladimir Petkovic.

Last Friday, the city's commercial court approved a request to restructure the debt as part of the club's continuation plan.

When Bordeaux were expelled from national-level football by the French FA at the start of the summer, the club used several avenues to appeal while the takeover was being finalised.

"We thought we had acquired the club in National 1 [the fourth tier]," Green and co-investor James Twining, told BBC Sport.

"Initially we walked away, but we were encouraged to come back," Green added. "We established that we were going to be able to restructure things and make it work.

"People around the club and in the local community encouraged us to try to find a way."

The six-time French champions have a long way to go before returning to the top flight.

"We're committing to a sensible financial structure, to a well-run club, and we're talking about 10 years to get this club back to Ligue 1," the new investors added.

A crucial step towards that long-term goal will be returning to the professional leagues, which would allow them to re-open the youth academy they were made to close when they dropped down.

Rebuilding the women's team, who were involved in the Champions League only a few seasons ago, is another one of the new owners' objectives.

Keeping the fans onside throughout the process will also be key, not least after the rift that opened up between groups during the previous ownership.

In any case, if the record-breaking turnout for Bordeaux's return to league action is anything to go by, their support seems unlikely to waver anytime soon.

articles.title: David Beckham spent years building a luxury empire, but his company is now suing fragrance distributor for at least $41 million after his perfumes allegedly ended up in gas station ‘bargain bin’
articles.summary: David Beckham's company, DB Ventures, is suing fragrance distributor Coty for at least $41 million, alleging damage to his luxury brand after his perfumes were discovered in discount retailers like Poundland.
articles.body: David Beckham has spent years building a commercial identity around fashion, lifestyle and luxury, with his name attached to everything from designer clothing to fragrances sold around the world. But his company says one of those carefully managed brand partnerships took an unexpected turn when his perfumes began appearing in Poundland and even a petrol station bargain bin. Now, the dispute has reached a New York court, with Beckham’s firm accusing the company behind the fragrances of damaging his brand and withholding millions in royalties.How Beckham’s fragrance partnership with Coty beganThe dispute centres on a licensing relationship between Beckham’s commercial company, DB Ventures, and beauty group Coty, which has produced and distributed fragrances and toiletries bearing the former England captain’s name for more than a decade.The original partnership dates back to March 2005, when Coty announced a global fragrance licensing agreement with David and Victoria Beckham. Beckham’s first signature fragrance followed later that year, beginning a relationship that eventually produced more than 30 different fragrances and related products.The arrangement was subsequently renewed in 2016 through an updated licensing agreement between DB Ventures and Coty. That contract set a royalty rate of 7% on fragrance sales and established rules governing where the products could be distributed and sold. Those provisions are now central to the legal dispute, with Beckham’s company arguing that Coty breached the agreement by allowing the fragrances to reach retailers that had not been approved.The range includes several recognisable lines, among them Classic, Instinct, Intimately and Exquisite Leather. In Britain, the fragrances typically sell for around £20 (approx. $26) a bottle, placing them within the accessible end of the designer fragrance market while still forming part of the lifestyle image Beckham’s company says it has worked to protect.The current licensing agreement is scheduled to run until March 31, 2028. However, DB Ventures has already agreed a new 20-year fragrance partnership with Interparfums, which is due to begin on April 1, 2028, or earlier if the Coty agreement is terminated. That future arrangement has become another point of contention, with Coty arguing that the lawsuit is an attempt by Beckham’s company to bring its existing deal to an early end and transfer the business to a new partner.From Poundland to a petrol station bargain binThe immediate dispute emerged after DB Ventures said it discovered Beckham-branded fragrances being sold through outlets that were not part of the agreed distribution network. Court documents describe products appearing at Poundland, the British discount retailer, as well as in what the company’s lawyers called a “bargain bin inside a gas station” at an unspecified location.The reaction from Beckham’s company was described in particularly strong terms. In its filing, DB Ventures said it had experienced “shock and dismay” upon discovering that products carrying his name were being sold in such locations, arguing that the association with heavily discounted retailers undermined the image it had spent years cultivating.The court papers state: “DB Ventures, the licensor of the David Beckham brand, ensures that all of its brand licensing partnerships maintain the lifestyle and luxury image of the brand that Sir David has carefully cultivated for decades.”The filing continued: “Imagine, then, the shock and dismay experienced when DB Ventures discovered that David Beckham products were being offered for sale in a gas station. How could this possibly have happened? Desperation and greed.”Lawyers for DB Ventures allege that Coty distributed at least $24 million (£18 million) worth of Beckham-branded products through unauthorised channels, including Poundland. They argue that selling the fragrances at what they describe as dollar-store prices associates the brand with cheap, discounted products and damages its carefully managed positioning.The complaint identifies the issue as more than a disagreement over individual retailers. Under the 2016 agreement, DB Ventures says, Coty was required to observe distribution conditions intended to protect the brand. The alleged sales, it argues, breached those obligations and exposed Beckham’s company to damage beyond the immediate value of the products involved.Coty has disputed the allegations. In its defence, the company denied that it had sold the fragrances in Poundland and argued that it was entitled to decide where it distributed the David Beckham range. It has also asked the court to dismiss the case, challenging whether New York courts have jurisdiction over the dispute.The $41 million lawsuit and the missing royaltiesThe disagreement also involves a substantial financial claim. DB Ventures is seeking at least $41 million in compensation and damages, alleging both unauthorised distribution and the under-reporting of fragrance sales.According to the court filing, Coty under-reported net sales by $123 million. DB Ventures says that discrepancy resulted in approximately $6 million in unpaid royalties under the 7% rate established by the 2016 agreement.The two allegations form the basis of the company's wider claim: that Coty not only allowed Beckham fragrances to reach outlets that threatened the brand's image but also failed to account properly for the sales generated by the licensing arrangement.Coty has rejected the claims and asked a judge to dismiss the lawsuit. Beyond disputing the allegations about Poundland, it argues that DB Ventures is using the proceedings to “manufacture its early exit” from the licensing agreement so that the Beckham fragrance business can move to Interparfums before the existing contract expires.The case was filed in April in the New York Supreme Court. In a statement to The Associated Press, Coty said: “Coty strongly disputes the claims and has asked the court to dismiss them. As this is an ongoing legal matter, we will not comment further.”DB Ventures’ parent company, Authentic Brands Group, declined to comment. The proceedings will determine whether the alleged distribution practices and accounting discrepancies amounted to breaches of the licensing agreement, while Coty’s jurisdiction challenge could affect where the dispute is heard.Beckham’s wider business empireThe fragrance dispute concerns one part of a much larger commercial operation built around Beckham’s name since his retirement from professional football in 2013. Through DRJB Holdings, Beckham has developed a business spanning brand partnerships, licensing and entertainment production.The group has three principal divisions. DB Ventures handles most of his commercial partnerships, including agreements with brands such as Hugo Boss. Seven Global oversees licensing arrangements with companies including Adidas, while Studio 99 is the production company responsible for projects such as the Netflix documentaries about David and Victoria Beckham.Beckham’s commercial profile has continued to expand through major international campaigns. He received a $51 million dividend from the group this year, following a series of lucrative partnerships connected to the FIFA World Cup. During the tournament, he appeared in around a dozen advertising campaigns for companies including Lenovo, McDonald’s and Bank of America.His business interests also extend into football, with Beckham a co-owner of Inter Miami, while his public profile has long included fashion, modelling and entertainment. He captained England, played for clubs including Manchester United and Real Madrid, and was knighted by King Charles III last year.The Sunday Times Rich List estimated the combined wealth of David and Victoria Beckham at almost £1.2 billion (approx. $1.58 billion) earlier this year. Their commercial interests have grown well beyond football, with the Beckham name now attached to a broad portfolio of businesses and licensing agreements.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Transfer news: Your Premier League club's unfinished business ahead of January window
articles.summary: Watch our 'Unfinished Business' Transfer Show special on Sky Sports News at 4pm and 7pm; the transfer window will re-open for Premier League clubs on January 1, 2027 and close on February 1 at 11pm; how many signings does your club need? Vote in our poll below
articles.body:
Arsenal failed to bring in a marquee forward in the summer and it remains one of their big objectives ahead of January as they prepare their recruitment plans for 2027.

The Premier League champions are understood to be tracking RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa and Brentford's Kevin Schade as potential options. Arsenal want a forward who primarily plays on the left but has the capability to feature across the front line.

Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez were pursued over the summer, but Arsenal failed to agree deals for any of their top forward targets.

Arsenal are believed to be moving on from Atletico Madrid's Alvarez as he is not keen to leave Spain. Meanwhile, Rogers signed for Chelsea in a £117m deal, a fee Arsenal were unwilling to reach, and Vinicius signed a new deal with Real Madrid.

Bournemouth's Alex Scott is also of interest to Arsenal, who are understood to be willing to move on a midfielder to beat Chelsea and Liverpool to the 23-year-old's signature.

Aston Villa ended the summer happy with their business after a window that, for a long time, looked like it would be a difficult one.

There were a host of high-profile departures but a string of arrivals to replace them have left Unai Emery with an exciting, younger squad and all positions filled.

One bit of unfinished business that will be arguably more important than the signing of any player is the new contract for manager Emery.

Bournemouth completed the business they planned to do over the summer transfer window and any further additions in January will likely depend on outgoings.

Alex Scott has interest from Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool with Bournemouth's stance over a potential sale softening since the summer having been unable to agree a new contract. It is understood Bournemouth would be seeking up to £100m, including add-ons.

Scott's departure is by no means a foregone conclusion in January but if he was to leave then Bournemouth would like to sign a midfielder.

Bournemouth want to ensure Marco Rose's squad is in a strong position to fight on in the Premier League and Europa League for the rest of the season before what is expected to be a big summer of upheaval.

Brentford are continuing to monitor Archie Gray's situation at Tottenham. The club were interested in signing him in the summer and are keeping an eye on his rate of minutes under Roberto De Zerbi.

Gray has been a focal point of De Zerbi's team so far this season, making eight starts in their 10 games. He has found an opening at right-back due to Pedro Porro's injury.

Porro returned to the starting line-up against Leeds, which saw Gray start in midfield, as Spurs were beaten at Elland Road. Brentford will be keeping an eye on whether Gray keeps his place or finds minutes harder to come-by in the run up to the January window.

Brentford are not expected to be busy in January having improved their squad in the summer and made an excellent start to the campaign under Keith Andrews

Brighton don't really have any "unfinished business" in terms of incomings from the summer to complete in January. They looked at a number of players in different positions and ended up signing a player in each role.

With Brighton's outstanding displays taking them to second in the table after 10 games, very little if anything is likely to happen in terms of first-team ready signings. Historically, owner/chair Tony Bloom prefers to do business in the summer when targets are more obtainable and more affordable than mid-season.

The January window is sometimes used to sign prospects from abroad and begin their development on the south coast. In terms of outgoings, they will not listen or entertain any offers for main first team squad players with the club being tipped as contenders for a Champions League place.

Some of the young players at the club may go out on loan for game time.

Manager Xabi Alonso remains open to signing another midfielder after the departure of Enzo Fernandez in the summer and seeing a Deadline Day deal for Monaco's Lamine Camara collapse.

Chelsea are interested in Bournemouth's Alex Scott and are believed to have the financial edge over other clubs in the race to sign the England international.

However, he is not Chelsea's only target while Romeo Lavia's improvement could reduce their urgency to reinforce their midfield options.

Coventry City made 12 major signings and spent over £130m during the summer, but results so far suggest further investment will be needed at both ends of the pitch to boost their chances of retaining Premier League status.

One situation to watch could be the future of attacking midfielder Jack Rudoni - a player Coventry will be determined to keep hold of but who is attracting attention after an impressive start to the season.

Club Brugge's Joel Ordonez saw his proposed summer move to Crystal Palace break down after he had a medical. The Ecuadorian is yet to play this season, so any renewed January move by the south London club is thought to be unlikely.

Palace signed centre-backs Axel Disasi from Chelsea and Honest Ahanor from Atalanta on loan, plus free agent defender Takehiro Tomiyasu, but further additions in that area, and also up front, cannot be ruled out.

Jean-Philippe Mateta's situation is one to watch too as he enters the final six months of his deal in January. Palace cashed in on Marc Guehi 12 months earlier before he became a summer free agent, and Palace may now have a similar dilemma over striker Mateta.

The threat of Premier League relegation - and the cost that comes with it - could also play a factor when deciding Mateta's future.

There will also be more talk about the future of Ismaila Sarr. He had his head turned by summer interest from Liverpool and then Galatasaray, while talks - described as "positive" and "good-natured" - have also taken place about extending the winger's contract, but a new agreement has yet to be confirmed.

Everton tried desperately to bring in a striker on Deadline Day. They were left frustrated when a move for Monaco's Folarin Balogun collapsed after the window closed having also failed with a loan bid for Joshua Zirkzee.

Thierno Barry's impressive form - 10 goals in 13 games this season - has softened the blow of missing out on a striker but he remains Everton's only out-and-out option up top, and a striker remains a priority.

Right-back was also a problem position for Everton. They have filled it this season with Merlin Rohl, Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Jake O'Brien but doubts remain about whether Everton have the role covered long term.

Fulham will closely monitor the transfer window for viable opportunities to improve their squad but do not currently feel they have any immediate need to reinforce in a single position.

With more midfielders than he can give game time to, head coach Alvaro Arbeloa may look to send a one or two out on loan.

Should Man Utd come in for centre back Calvin Bassey, Fulham may be forced to enter the market. Although it would require a very big fee to convince them to part ways with such an important player and leader.

Arbeloa has said Fulham are keen to agree a contract extension with Bassey to keep him in west London.

Hull City recruited heavily in the summer and are expected to have a much quieter January transfer window. But one area where they may look to strengthen is on the left side of their attack.

They continue to assess the fitness of Ilyas Ansah, who has been sidelined with a back injury since joining in the summer. Ansah has yet to make his competitive debut but could return to training next month. Several fringe players could also leave the club in this window.

Ipswich Town went big in the summer in a bid to have all angles covered on their return to the Premier League. After splashing out over £200m on 16 players they had the second-highest net-spend (£190.7m) in the Premier League behind Liverpool (£219.4m).

Their chairman Mark Ashton told Sky Sports News : "We have never shied away from the transfer market. We were very aggressive in the summer but if the right things come along we will look at them in the right way."

Leeds United are happy with the current state of their squad after addressing the key areas of need in the summer transfer window, but will remain open to market opportunities in January.

There was interest over the summer in signing a striker who could support Dominic Calvert-Lewin, with a younger profile viewed as ideal.

Leeds tried to sign Jorgen Strand Larsen for a then club-record fee last January, but there is no longer any appetite to bring in a player that would potentially limit Calvert-Lewin's role.

Sky Sports News understands Calvert-Lewin is expected to extend his stay at Elland Road beyond his current deal, which has 18 months to run. There was interest from Manchester United but they have no plans to explore a potential move further.

Liverpool were interested in Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr and Brighton's Yankuba Minteh late in the summer window but were unable to sign either winger.

Any renewed move will depend largely on whether their clubs are more open to doing business than they were in the summer though Liverpool's plans are yet to be firmed up.

With Sarr and Minteh staying put, Cody Gakpo remained at Anfield despite interest from Manchester City and Tottenham.

That left head coach Andoni Iraola with the pool of five wide options that he ideally wants, though that does include Federico Chiesa who has only been a bit-part player this season.

Manchester City will be braced for any interest that comes in Rayan Ait-Nouri this January, given Manchester United tried to sign him on loan on Deadline Day.

But they are not making any decisions on the former Wolves left-back given there is still more than a month to go until the window opens and they may need all their players.

Ait-Nouri has not played a single minute in the Premier League so far and has failed to even make the squad for four of City's 10 games.

Meanwhile, City are not looking to sign Malo Gusto, Sky Sports News understands, amid widespread reports about the right-back's future at Chelsea.

City have reportedly been interested in Gusto given boss Enzo Maresca worked with him at Stamford Bridge - but that is not the case.

Right-back is a position City have been assessing whether or not to strengthen further for some time but have been looking at younger development players such as Feyenoord's Givairo Read.

Man Utd prioritised the midfield rebuild over signing a left-back and striker in the summer but, after their worst start to a league season for 40 years, there is an acknowledgement from the hierarchy that they could have strengthened further in the last window.

New head coach Mauricio Pochettino, who replaced the sacked Michael Carrick last week, is expected to be backed in January and have input on potential targets with left-back, centre-back and a forward on the agenda.

Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite and Fulham's Calvin Bassey are among the left-sided defenders being monitored with Lisandro Martinez's future in doubt. The Argentina international is into the final year of his deal, which includes an option for a further 12 months.

Forward options are being explored with Benjamin Sesko, the club's only recognised No 9, out injured until at least January, while left-back cover is another potential area of focus with five different players used in that position this season with limited success.

Matthias Jaissle wants to add more goals to his team this January, with a No 9 and a No 10 top of his wish list.

He doesn't have an out-and-out No 10 in his current squad, despite persisting with the 4-2-3-1 formation since he joined the club in the summer.

Joe Willock and Yoane Wissa have both been deployed in that position so far, but neither is natural in that role.

However, the chances of signing players for both positions are slim, unless Newcastle offset that with sales.

The winter window is notoriously difficult to operate in, with difference makers being the hardest players to sign.

Signing a player for one of those positions is likely to be as good as Newcastle can achieve, given the financial restraints.

Jaissle wants to add experience in January, having lost a clutch of experienced players in the summer. This will be his first window to operate in, having arrived late in the summer.

Ivan Toney is one striker he admires and would like to sign, having managed him previously with Al Ahli, but he knows it is unlikely to make economic sense for a club trying to invest in younger players with high ceilings.

Central midfield and goalkeeper are two positions outstanding from the summer that Nottingham Forest could look at if they go back into the market in January.

Forest were prepared to spend big in midfield but were unsuccessful with offers for Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall, Everton's Harrison Armstrong and Liverpool's Trey Nyoni.

It was a similar story in goal. Forest were linked with Crystal Palace's Dean Henderson, Chelsea's Robert Sanchez and Liverpool's Giorgi Mamardashvili but did not sign any of them.

The form of Oliver Glasner's players and team between now and January will determine which situations Forest revisit in the winter window.

Sunderland were frantically trying to add to their squad on Deadline Day and winger Malick Fofana was their main arrival from Lyon. They were keen to add another winger and tried for Benfica's Dodi Lukebakio but failed to secure his signature.

Head coach Regis Le Bris also wanted an additional attacker, to give him another genuine option behind Brian Brobbey and Wilson Isidor. Sunderland signed teenage prospect Juan Riquelme Angulo to plug that gap but he has barely featured this season, leaving that as one role they may still want to fill.

Tottenham were one of the Premier League's biggest spenders in the summer with an outlay of more than £330m on new signings but that does not rule out the possibility of a fresh addition in the January transfer window.

Goals have been an issue for Roberto De Zerbi's side this season, with only two Premier League sides scoring fewer after 10 matches, and Spurs are open to bringing in another forward if the right player becomes available.

Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi was a target in the summer before his metatarsal injury ruled him out for the first three months of the season. The 20-year-old has now returned to action, but it would take a huge fee to prise him from Bournemouth in January.

Spurs will also seek to find a new club for Richarlison, who rejected a move to Everton at the end of the summer window after he was omitted from De Zerbi's Premier League squad. The Brazilian, whose contract is up in the summer, has not played for the first team since August.

articles.standfirst: Una nueva hornada de jóvenes talentos comienza brillar en el fútbol de selecciones
articles.summary: Una nueva hornada de jóvenes talentos comienza brillar en el fútbol de selecciones
articles.body: El Mundial 2026 dio paso a una 'nueva era' en el fútbol de selecciones. La retirada, a nivel internacional, de figuras de la talla de Cristiano Ronaldo, Leo Messi, Neymar, Manuel Neuer, James Rodríguez, Romelu Lukaku, Edin Dzeko... ha dado paso a una nueva hornada de jóvenes talentos que han comenzado a 'derribar la puerta', en especial, en este último parón. Demarcación: Mediapunta. Edad: 22 años. Altura: 1,78. Pie: Zurdo. El extremo del RB Leipzig, cedido por el Brighton, es, seguramente, el caso más significativo. No había debutado aún con la absoluta de Alemania y sale del parón convertido en uno de los referentes del nuevo proyecto que lidera Jürgen Klopp. Marcó en su estreno ante Serbia (1-3) y fabricó tres goles -anotó uno y repartió dos asistencias- en la 'manita' a Países Bajos (5-0). “Es un talento extraordinario. No voy a ser el diablo y prohibirle que regatee”, aseguró el nuevo seleccionador de la 'Mannschaft'. Demarcación: Delantero. Edad: 20 años. Altura: 1,79. Pie: Diestro. Roberto Martínez trató de convencer sin éxito al atacante del Bournemouth para que representara a Portugal. "Quería representar a Francia, así que lo respetamos", aseguró 'Bob'. No estuvo en el Mundial y Zinedine Zidane le incluyó de urgencia en su última lista por la lesión de Marcus Thuram. Su impacto, sin embargo, fue inmediato. Debutó -jugó los últimos 13'- en la derrota ante Italia (3-1) y marcó su primer gol, saliendo desde el banquillo, en la victoria ante Turquía (2-1). "Quería demostrar de lo que era capaz. Descubrir la selección francesa era un sueño para mí. Y marcar un gol es simplemente increíble", reconocía el excanterano del Lorient. Demarcación: Mediapunta. Edad: 17 años. Altura: 1,84. Pie: Diestro. Lo tenía hecho con el Real Madrid... pero un problema en el reconocimiento médico tiró por tierra su fichaje. Ahora brilla en el Ajax con Míchel: suma tres goles y cinco asistencias en apenas 788'. También con Marruecos. Marcó a pase de Brahim Díaz el gol de la victoria ante Níger (1-0), convirtiéndose en el jugador más joven (17 años y 306 días) en marcar con la absoluta de los 'Leones del Atlas' a lo largo de la historia. "No puedo expresar con palabras lo feliz que estoy. Me alegra haber contribuido a la clasificación de la selección marroquí para la Copa África", aseguró. Un parón especial, también, para Yassir Zabiri. La gran revelación de LaLiga -acumula nueve goles en 12 partidos con el Racing- también se estrenó como goleador con Marruecos. Fue en la victoria en el primer partido ante Níger (5-1). Demarcación: Extremo. Edad: 22 años. Altura: 1,79. Pie: Zurdo. Otra 'joya' que se le ha escapado a Portugal. Nació en Bélgica... pero llegó a ser internacional sub 21 con la 'Seleçao das Quinas'. Rudi García le dio la alternativa con los 'diablos rojos' hace un año y se lo llevó al Mundial... pero ha terminado explotando a las órdenes de Mark van Bommel. El extremo del Milan, fichado este verano del Estrasburgo a cambio de 50 millones, debutó como goleador en la victoria ante Italia (4-1). "Estoy muy feliz por mi primer gol con la selección. Espero marcar más. Fue un momento especial porque estaba mi familia. Es un día que recordaré para siempre", afirmó el excanterano del Benfica. Demarcación: Extremo. Edad: 22 años. Altura: 1,69. Pie: Zurdo. El 'adeus' de Cristiano Ronaldo dejó un vacío imposible de llenar. "Ha llegado el día de devolver la camiseta siete de la selección de todos nosotros", anunció. Un '7' que, ante la lesión de Rafael Leao, recayó sobre Carlos Forbs. El extremo del Brujas -jugó los últimos 26'- no pudo evitar el bochorno frente a Dinamarca (1-4)... pero se vistió de 'salvador' en el triunfo 'in extremis' en Gales (2-3). En un momento en el que parecía peligrar el liderato del grupo, el ex del Manchester City marcó con una conducción 'marca de la casa': tiró la diagonal hacia adento y se sacó un tiro al palo largo con la zurda. "No diría que es una presión, pero está claro que es un número especial. Estoy muy orgulloso de representar este dorsal", reconocía. Demarcación: Delantero. Edad: 20 años. Altura: 1,84. Pie: Diestro. El atacante del Sion, que suma 13 goles y cinco asistencias en los 18 partidos que ha disputado esta temporada, vivió su primer gran noche con Suiza en la goleada sobre Escocia (4-0). En su primer partido como titular -había jugado otros tres como suplente- marcó su primer gol con la absoluta y repartió su primera asistencia. "Es instinto de delantero; siempre quiere estar en el lugar correcto en el momento justo", subrayó el seleccionador Murat Yakin. Demarcación: Mediapunta. Edad: 20 años. Altura: 1,78. Pie: Diestro. El nombre propio del parón en Italia ha sido, sin duda, Pio Esposito. El joven '9' del Inter acumula 10 goles en 15 internacionalidades con la 'Azzurra'. Cabe destacar, sin embargo, el debut con la 'Nazionale' de la nueva joya del Milan: Alphadjo Cisse. Se quedó fuera de la lista en la victoria ante Francia (3-1) en San Siro... pero disputó los últimos 26' -sustituyó a Scalvini en el 62'- en la derrota ante Bélgica (4-1). Y fue uno de los más destacados: rozó el gol con un cabezazo que salió desviado en el 86', provocó el penalti que falló Esposito en el 89' y vio cómo le anulaban un gol por fuera de juego en el 95'. Demarcación: Extremo. Edad: 16 años. Altura: 1,83. Pie: Zurdo. El 'niño prodigio' del Arsenal ha sumado un nuevo récord. Ya era el jugador más joven en marcar (16 años y 73 días) en Premier y en debutar en Champions (15 años y 308 días). Dowman ha sumado otras dos plusmarcas en este parón: ha desbancado a Jude Bellingham como el debutante (16 años y 320 días) y el goleador (16 años y 323 días) más precoz con la sub 21 inglesa. "Es un chico extraordinario. Casi te olvidas de la edad que tiene", señala su compañero Mikey Moore. Demarcación: Mediapunta. Edad: 17 años. Altura: 1,80. Pie: Zurdo. Otro futbolista muy codiciado. Nacido en Martigues (Francia), ha sido internacional con Portugal desde la sub 16. En la victoria ante Noruega (1-0) dio un paso más: se convirtió en el segundo jugador más joven (17 años y 9 días) en marcar con la sub 21 de Portugal. "Me alegré mucho por Mezian. Demostró crecimiento y madurez, marcó el gol y podría haber marcado otro más", aseveró Luís Freire para referirse al extremo del Lens, que ya dejó una gran sensación en la remontada en Champions ante el Slavia Praga (2-3). Demarcación: Mediapunta. Edad: 22 años. Altura: 1,85. Pie: Zurdo. El excanterano del Real Madrid ni debutaba... ni se estrenaba como goleador. Es evidente, sin embargo, que, tras la retirada de Leo Messi, ha dado un paso al frente. El '10' del Como se 'echó el equipo a la espalda' en la derrota ante Uruguay (1-2) y se reivindicó en la goleada ante Costa Rica (7-0) con un doblete. "Lo único que tengo en mente es disfrutar de días como hoy. No hay nada como divertirse en la cancha, haciendo lo que más amo: jugar al fútbol. Y el verdadero orgullo es hacerlo representando a esta camiseta, a la Selección y a tanta gente que nos apoya. Yo juego para esto", aseguró Nico Paz, que suma seis goles en 16 internacionalidades, cuando le preguntaron por la posibilidad de heredar el '10' de Messi. También firmó dos goles -acumula tres en ocho partidos con la absoluta- Franco Mastantuono. “Es uno de los que tenemos que llevar poco a poco. Estoy convencido de que hay que tranquilizarlo, ayudarlo y que será un gran futbolista”, afirmó Leonel Scaloni. Demarcación: Delantero. Edad: 18 años. Altura: 1,78. Pie: Diestro. Al igual que en el caso de Nico Paz, no era su estreno. Sin embargo, conviene destacar el impacto que ha tenido en el combinado de las 'barras y estrellas'. El atacante de NY Red Bulls suma cinco goles en seis partidos desde su debut a las órdenes de Mauricio Pochettino. En el doble compromiso ante Haití en los cuartos de final de la Nations League de la CONCACAF volvió a dejar su sello: marcó un gol en la ida (6-0) y otro en la vuelta (2-0). "No esperaba estar donde estoy ahora mismo con 18 años. Para mí, todo consistía en hacer lo máximo posible para llegar a ser profesional", reconoce.

articles.title: El Barcelona busca reencontrarse: "Ya nos pondréis las notas más adelante"
articles.standfirst: Recibe al Servette tras encadenar dos empates de manera consecutiva
articles.summary: Recibe al Servette tras encadenar dos empates de manera consecutiva
articles.body: El Barcelona llega a la quinta jornada de la fase Liga de la UWCL tras encadenar dos malos resultados (dos empates), algo que no sucedía desde hace siete años. De ahí que llame la atención. Sin embargo, Pere Romeu, su técnico, quiso ayer apagar cualquier tipo de alarma. "Estamos en noviembre, la temporada es larguísima. Ya nos pondréis las notas más adelante, pero este equipo lo dará todo para luchar por todos los títulos", apuntó antes de recibir al Servette este jueves (21:00 horas) en el Johan Cruyff. El calendario y las lesiones han lastrado la evolución de un equipo que incorpora cada vez más talento joven. "Empezamos la temporada con una plantilla muy corta. Luego encadenas periodos competitivos, algunas futbolistas se caen durante el proceso y tienes pocas opciones de rotar", explicó. "Jugando cada tres días es complicado mantener el tono físico y más en la situación en la que estamos con jugadoras lesionadas que nos ayudarían a entrar en rotaciones y tener piernas más frescas", justificó. Más allá de las excusas, Romeu es consciente de que a nivel deportivo el equipo está para más. "No hemos estado tan perfectos como solemos estarlo", dijo. "Las acciones de metros finales no las hemos resuelto del todo bien. No solo las ocasiones falladas, sino las acciones previas: los pases, las paredes, el desequilibrio...", añadió quien ya piensa en sacarse la espina en el próximo duelo. "El Servette vendrá aquí a muerte, a darlo todo e intentar rascar todo lo posible. Vamos a tener dificultades", avisó. Romeu dijo no estar valorando incorporaciones en el mercado de invierno, sino recuperar inquilinas de la enfermería y seguir dando paso a las jóvenes. "No pienso ahora en el mercado, pienso en recuperar a las futbolistas que están fuera. Y hay futbolistas de abajo que seguirán teniendo oportunidades porque tienen mucha calidad", subrayó. "No pretendamos que el primer día derriben la puerta. Estoy convencido de que hay futbolistas de abajo que seguirán teniendo oportunidades y tienen mucha calidad", sentenció.

articles.title: El Barça respira tras el parón
articles.standfirst: Solo Livakovic y Gordon acumularon bastantes minutos; el resto de culés, sin mucha carga
articles.summary: Solo Livakovic y Gordon acumularon bastantes minutos; el resto de culés, sin mucha carga
articles.body: El Barcelona puso el martes por la noche el punto final al parón internacional de noviembre, una ventana que los azulgranas han cerrado sin tanta acumulación de minutos como en otras ocasiones. De hecho, únicamente un jugador del Barça ha completado los 180 minutos posibles: Livaković. Sin embargo, el guardameta croata no es titular, por lo que su elevada carga de minutos no supone un contratiempo para el técnico alemán. Gordon es el segundo azulgrana que más tiempo ha permanecido sobre el terreno de juego, con un total de 160 minutos. El internacional inglés fue titular en los encuentros contra Croacia y España, aunque no llegó a completar ninguno de los dos. El siguiente en la lista es Pau Cubarsí, que ha acumulado 135'. El central catalán, que está entre algodones por una sobrecarga muscular, disputó los 90' del encuentro contra la República Checa, pero tuvo que abandonar el terreno de juego en el descanso del choque contra Inglaterra después de notar molestias. Fermín López también ha tenido protagonismo con la selección española. El centrocampista ha sumado 127 minutos, repartidos entre los 82 que disputó en el primer compromiso y la segunda mitad del segundo encuentro. Por su parte, Marc Bernal regresa a la Ciudad Condal después de acumular 126 minutos con la sub-21. El canterano, con un rol menos protagonista en el Barcelona, ha aprovechado esta convocatoria para seguir sumando minutos. Lamine Yamal, por su parte, únicamente pudo participar en uno de los dos compromisos de España. El delantero se perdió el encuentro contra la República Checa por unas molestias físicas, pero sí estuvo disponible para el duelo contra Inglaterra. Ante los británicos disputó los 90 minutos y volvió a dejar su sello, provocando un penalti y repartiendo una asistencia. Cancelo también tuvo una participación limitada. El portugués disputó los 90 minutos del encuentro contra Gales de ayer martes, después de perderse el primer compromiso de su selección por sanción. Raphinha, en cambio, se quedó en únicamente 71 minutos con Brasil. El extremo azulgrana fue protagonista en el encuentro contra Japón, aunque después de ser sustituido, vio la tarjeta roja y se perdió el segundo cruce. Pedri, mientras tanto, acumuló 60 minutos con España. De Jong sumó solo 45 con Países Bajos. En el caso del neerlandés, su participación estuvo condicionada por unas molestias físicas. Pese a ello, las previsiones apuntan a que podrá estar disponible para el encuentro contra el Villarreal de este domingo. En el apartado de los internacionales con aún menos protagonismo aparece Hamza Abdelkarim, que apenas disputó 15 minutos en el empate sin goles de Egipto contra Malawi. Joan Garcia, por su parte, fue el único de los convocados que regresó sin haber sumado minutos durante el parón. En definitiva, el Barcelona cierra esta ventana internacional con un balance relativamente positivo en cuanto al desgaste de su plantilla. Más allá de las situaciones físicas de Cubarsí y De Jong, la mayoría de los futbolistas importantes para Hansi Flick han tenido una carga de minutos moderada.

articles.title: Paul McStay: Fan voice on board key to ending Celtic unrest
articles.summary: Celtic legend Paul McStay says having a supporters representative on the board would be a significant step to halting the unrest between the club and the fans.
articles.body:
Celtic legend Paul McStay says having a supporters representative on the board would be a significant step to halting the unrest between the club and the fans.

Issues have arisen around a perceived lack of investment in the Scottish Premiership outfit and underachievement in Europe, with one prominent supporters group recently boycotting matches in protest.

Former Scotland international McStay played his entire club career at Celtic, making more than 500 league appearances between 1981 and 1997 and winning three league titles, four Scottish Cups and a League Cup.

Now he is involved with a collection of season-ticket holders, whose aim is to have more say in how the club is run.

The former captain has made his opinion known to members of the board and believes "healthy debate" can resolve the "disconnect".

Why Celtic's next three games could set AGM tone

"I think there's issues that have to be resolved just now," McStay said. "When Celtic players, management, directors and supporters are all as one, we will be successful or have a great chance of being successful so my hope is that happens again.

"To me, it's healthy debate that's required and come up with a solution that helps our drive forward - domestically maintain the success and in Europe. I think that's what the fans want."

In just under a fortnight, Celtic shareholders will gather at the ground for the club's annual general meeting.

Given the chaos of last year's event, there will be extra eyes and ears on the 2026 AGM on 1 December. And McStay wants change to try and avert more problems.

"The idea is to get enough equity in the club to allow the supporters to have a representative on the board and to me that's important.

"I know the directors and they just want the best for Celtic. We are allowed opinions and I voice my opinions to them, slightly different from what they're thinking.

"To have regular Champions League football is what Celtic supporters are hoping for and I think we can achieve that. But just now I think there's a few things that need to be talked about, debated and hopefully we can move forward as a club."
