articles.title: Alex Scott: Arsenal keen on Chelsea and Liverpool target with Bournemouth softening stance over potential sale
articles.summary: Premier League champions Arsenal would require a sale to accommodate Alex Scott in their midfield and it is understood they would be willing to make a change in that department to beat rivals Chelsea and Liverpool to the 23-year-old's signature with Bournemouth demanding up to £100m
articles.body:
Sky Sports News understands the Premier League champions would be willing to make changes in midfield to beat Chelsea and Liverpool to the 23-year-old's signature.

Discussions about Arsenal's 2027 transfer plans are believed to have taken place between manager Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta already.

It is understood they would need to sell at least one of their current midfielders to facilitate a deal for Scott in January or next summer.

With Declan Rice , Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly all doing so well this season, Mikel Merino is arguably the most likely candidate having struggled for game time. He has made only one Premier League start and said last week while on Spain duty that he wants more minutes.

His club and country team-mate Martin Zubimendi could be another candidate, although illness and injury have impacted his minutes so far this campaign and he has impressed recently when he has played. There is still a long way to go in the season and any injury to a key midfielder could impact Arsenal's ideas.

Merino said while on Spain duty: "We know what our roles are, and we're both calm and eager to keep training hard to show that we can continue to be there." But he also said: "Not being on the pitch most of the time isn't ideal for a player. Arsenal is currently the best team in the world, and it's very difficult to get minutes."

Scott is likely to be one of the biggest names potentially on the January transfer market, with Bournemouth believed to have softened their stance on the idea of a sale, having been unable to agree a new contract with the 23-year-old.

However, they will still command a high fee for the England international, hoping for close to £100m including add-ons. Sources have indicated something around £75m to £80m plus bonuses could get a deal done.

Bournemouth are also going strongly this season however, including in the Europa League. Should that continue, they may feel keeping Scott until next summer would give them a better chance of going far in the competition and securing European football again for next season.

Chelsea also remain persistent with their interest in Scott, and they are believed to have the financial edge on other clubs - but he is not their only target.

Manager Xabi Alonso remains open to signing another midfielder after the departure of Enzo Fernandez in the summer, although Romeo Lavia's improvement has lessened the necessity, after seeing a deadline-day deal for Lamine Camara of Monaco fall down in the summer.

Liverpool are keen to add to their midfield options in the longer term, and they see Scott as the perfect option to add some guile and passing ability to their squad.

Scott was a key part of Andoni Iraola's system at Bournemouth before the Spanish coach moved to Anfield. He remains a big admirer and there is a wider belief at Liverpool that he could also be a key tactical piece in Iraola's plans going forward.

Scott will have only 12 months left on his existing deal next summer, at which point his value will reduce.

Arsenal tracking Nusa and Schade in winger search

Latest from Sky Sports News' Adrian Kajumba and Lyall Thomas:

Arsenal are continuing to track the likes of RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa and Brentford's Kevin Schade as they assess potential forward options ahead of improving their squad in 2027.

Adding a marquee name to their attack was one of the objectives Arsenal were unable to tick-off during the summer window, failing to agree deals for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Jr, Bradley Barcola and Julian Alvarez.

With Alvarez not keen to leave Spain, the Gunners are believed to be moving on from their pursuit of the Argentina star and assessing again how to improve in attack, primarily on the left side but with someone versatile enough to operate across the frontline.

A move for Nusa is now something Arsenal are keen to progress with, sources have told Sky Sports News , but he is not the only potential target they are monitoring.

Sky Sports News revealed their admiration for Schade last month amid the forward's talks with Brentford over a new contract.

Nusa, who has two-and-a-half years left on his Leipzig deal, has no exit clause so a deal would need to be negotiated - and Leipzig do not want to sell him January come-what-may, according to other sources, so a move next summer seems more feasible as things stand.

Nusa actually almost signed for Brentford in the summer they brought in Schade from Freiburg.

Nicknamed the Norwegian Neymar after his childhood hero, Nusa is an international team-mate of Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard and has been on the radar of Premier League clubs for some time.

He is now into his third season and producing his best performances to date. The 21-year-old has directly contributed to 14 goals in just 15 games in all competitions this season, with six goals and eight assists.

One of his goals was a Champions League strike against Manchester City earlier this month and this season's efforts add to the 10 goals and 11 assists he recorded across his first two seasons at the German club.

articles.title: Urban Meyer Eyed as New HC Target for Big Ten Team, Latest Rumors Reveal amid Brian Kelly Buzz
articles.summary: After former LSU head coach Brian Kelly was reported as a top candidate for Maryland's head coach opening, another option has emerged.
articles.body:
After former LSU head coach Brian Kelly was reported as a top candidate for Maryland's head coach opening, another option has emerged.

Jeff Ermann of 247Sports reported that sources said former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer has spoken with Maryland athletic director Jim Smith about the job with the Terrapins.

Maryland fired head coach Mike Locksley last month after a 2-5 start this season and 12 consecutive losses in Big Ten play dating back to 2025. Aazaar Abdul-Rahim took over as the team's interim coach, and the Terps have since improved to 4-6.

In addition to coaching at Ohio State from 2012 to 2018, Meyer served as head coach at Florida, Utah and Bowling Green. He led the Gators to national championships in 2006 and 2008, and he led the Buckeyes to the 2014 national title. He hasn't coached since his failed NFL stint with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2021, in which he was fired after going 2-11 in 13 games. He's served as an analyst for Fox Sports since then.

Ermann noted that a source with knowledge of Meyer's discussion with Smith said the 62-year-old "would like something to add a more positive page to the end of his resume." He reportedly "has a warm relationship" with Smith and "also shares a relationship with Maryland deputy AD Diana Sabau."

Kelly has already interviewed with the Terps, so he could have a slight lead in the race. Ermann added that it's "unclear if Meyer has been offered the job or whether he'd accept if so, and the university would need to make a massive new investment in football to lure Meyer and a top staff, along with an expected NIL and revenue-sharing budget increase that sources have said will have Maryland's roster in the $30-35 million range next season."

It's apparent that the Terps are hoping to land a big-name hire as they enter a new era, but it remains to be seen if they will be able to convince Meyer to take the job.

articles.title: Se busca un central y un lateral
articles.standfirst: Flick quiere reforzar la defensa en enero y en verano
articles.summary: Flick quiere reforzar la defensa en enero y en verano
articles.body: Después de dos Ligas ganadas de manera consecutiva con Hansi Flick en el banquillo, el gran reto del Barcelona es el asalto a la Champions. En esos dos años cayó ante el Inter y el Atlético de Madrid en semifinales y cuartos de final, respectivamente. Dos eliminatorias que demostraron que el equipo necesita mejorar en defensa si quiere llegar a lo más alto, porque recibió diez goles en esos cuatro partidos. Haber encadenado 18 partidos consecutivos encajando goles en la Champions, hasta el 3-0 ante el Aston Villa, también es un dato preocupante. Por este motivo, la Dirección Deportiva del Barcelona trabaja desde ahora en la mejora de la línea defensiva, con el beneplácito de Flick, que actualmente sí quiere refuerzos en la retaguardia después de que en verano optase por no reforzar el centro de la defensa. Una decisión de reforzar que tomó junto a Deco después de las dos derrotas consecutivas ante el PSG y el Real Madrid, que demostraron que al equipo le falta solvencia defensiva cuando se enfrenta a grandes rivales. Flick quiere reforzar la zaga con dos jugadores: un central y un lateral. El primer objetivo está en el centro de la zaga. El Barcelona necesita un defensa central potente que pueda hacer pareja con Pau Cubarsí, un futbolista intocable hoy y durante muchos años. Gerard Martín está mejorando, pero todavía le falta para alcanzar un alto nivel. Y con Christensen se puede contar a cuentagotas debido a las continuas lesiones que sufre. Además, Eric García está jugando más de lateral que de central y es un perfil muy parecido al de Cubarsí. Koundé, otra de las alternativas debido a su pasado como central, no atraviesa en este momento un buen estado de forma y el club estaría dispuesto a aceptar una oferta si se diera el caso. Y lo de Koundé enlaza con la necesidad de reforzar la banda. La apuesta del Barcelona por los laterales no ha salido bien. Koundé estaba llamado a convertirse en un fijo por la banda derecha, pero lleva tiempo sin estar a su mejor nivel. Lo sabe el jugador y lo sabe la Dirección Deportiva. Por la otra banda, Balde tampoco está al nivel que Flick exige a sus laterales y lleva así temporada y media. Por este motivo, está en venta y saldrá en el mercado de invierno. Ante esta situación, Flick ha tenido que echar mano de su imaginación para compensar el bajo rendimiento de estos jugadores. La pasada campaña recuperó a Joao Cancelo, pero el portugués, a sus 32 años, es una solución momentánea y no una apuesta de futuro. El entrenador ha tirado de la cantera con Xavi Espart y Brian Fariñas, que han estado jugando de laterales en lo que llevamos de temporada: el primero desde agosto y el segundo tras la lesión de Koundé. Ambos han rendido a buen nivel, pero no hay que olvidar que son centrocampistas reconvertidos a laterales. Pueden desempeñar una buena función defensiva y ayudar a reforzar la medular, pero les falta profundidad para llegar por banda a la portería rival. Por todo esto, urge la llegada de un lateral que, salvo sorpresa, no será en enero. La idea es ficharlo en verano para incorporarlo la próxima campaña. Uno de los nombres que ha sonado es Pedro Porro. Es un futbolista que gusta en Can Barça y de categoría contrastada. Campeón del mundo con España, lleva varias temporadas rindiendo a un excelente nivel en el Tottenham. Es una operación complicada por su coste: su valor de mercado está entre 40 y 50 millones de euros y acaba de renovar su contrato con el club inglés hasta 2031.

articles.title: Elevan el listón de Güler al de una leyenda del Real Madrid: "Está en camino de superar a..."
articles.standfirst: Tote en Despierta San Francisco le comparó con Guti
articles.summary: Tote en Despierta San Francisco le comparó con Guti
articles.body: Tote pasó por los micrófonos de 'Despierta San Francisco', de Radio MARCA, para repasar diferentes asuntos de la actualidad futbolística. Uno de los nombres propios de la conversación fue Arda Güler, cuya continuidad en el Real Madrid valoró muy positivamente. El exfutbolista no escatimó en elogios hacia el centrocampista turco, al que ve como uno de esos jugadores capaces de marcar diferencias gracias a su talento. "Es el Guti de este Real Madrid. Todavía no llega a Guti, pero está en camino. Es un jugador distinto y una muy buena noticia para el Madrid y para los que les gusta el fútbol porque es un tipo que te hace disfrutar", explicó. También tuvo que elegir entre Güler y Nico Paz, dos futbolistas que representan un perfil creativo y diferente dentro del terreno de juego. Tote reconoció las virtudes de ambos, aunque considera que el turco tiene algo que necesita especialmente el conjunto blanco. "Arda Güler tiene mejor último pase y Nico tiene más gol y más llegada. Depende de lo que quiera el Madrid y del equipo que tenga", señaló antes de decantarse claramente por el otomano: "Arda Güler ahora mismo para mí es imprescindible. Creo que al Madrid no le hace tanta falta el gol como el último pase. Me parece que es el más importante ahora mismo". Sobre Nico Paz, que ha experimentado una importante evolución desde su salida del Real Madrid, también tuvo buenas palabras. Tote considera que su etapa junto a Cesc Fàbregas en el Como le ha permitido crecer y desarrollar sus cualidades. "Le ha venido muy bien estar con Cesc porque tengo la sensación de que Cesc saca mucho partido a ese prototipo de jugador, a ese jugador talentoso, con último pase distinto y que lleva la cabeza levantada", comentó. Además, destacó que actualmente está preparado para asumir retos importantes y que todavía tiene margen de crecimiento. Otro de los asuntos que abordó fue la posible llegada de JJ Gabriel al Real Madrid. El joven futbolista de 16 años, que prepara su salida del Manchester United, ha generado un importante ruido mediático después de despedirse del club inglés. Tote, sin embargo, considera que la responsabilidad de gestionar este tipo de situaciones no debe recaer únicamente en los propios jugadores, todavía en una edad de formación. "El problema ya no son los chicos, porque los chicos tienen edad para equivocarse y para tener pajaritos en la cabeza. El problema es el entorno que tengas", afirmó. El exfutbolista puso especialmente el foco en los representantes y en la influencia que pueden llegar a tener en las decisiones de los jóvenes talentos. "Muchas veces los representantes van donde más les dan a ellos, pero no donde el chico, por sus cualidades, puede triunfar más", explicó. Para Tote, a la hora de elegir un destino resulta fundamental estudiar el perfil del jugador, los entrenadores y la idea futbolística de cada club, por encima de las condiciones económicas. Una reflexión que también nace de su propia experiencia profesional. El exjugador reconoció que durante su carrera tuvo varios representantes y que no siempre quedó satisfecho con su trabajo. "Me han engañado. Me han prometido cosas que luego no han cumplido", confesó. Incluso recordó que, en alguna ocasión, llegó a enterarse por presidentes de otros clubes de que habían estado interesados en contratarle, pero que las exigencias económicas de su representante habían terminado frustrando las operaciones. "Hay veces que haces las cosas muy bien y el representante de turno no te sabe colocar, no tiene la fuerza suficiente para ir a un club y decir: 'A este chico respondo yo por él'", añadió. Tote considera que el fútbol ha llegado a una situación en la que algunos intermediarios tienen demasiado protagonismo: "Hay veces que el representante tiene más fuerza que incluso el jugador que juega. Eso es el mundo al revés". Por último, también analizó la derrota de la selección española frente a Inglaterra. Lejos de mostrar preocupación, Tote reconoció el mérito del combinado inglés, al que vio muy superior durante buena parte del encuentro. "Me pareció que Inglaterra me impresionó. No me creía que iba a jugar de esa manera. Hizo un primer tiempo y diez minutos del segundo muy superior a España", valoró. El exfutbolista destacó especialmente el nivel de Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane y Anthony Gordon, tres futbolistas que considera determinantes en el potencial inglés. "Bellingham me pareció que está a un nivel altísimo, Harry Kane tiene mucho fútbol y Gordon, cuando tiene el balón, te mata porque tiene muy bien el espacio-tiempo", explicó. Eso sí, también recordó que Inglaterra sigue teniendo una asignatura pendiente en las grandes citas internacionales, donde considera que le ha faltado personalidad para dar el último paso. "De calidad y de físico lo tiene todo para ser protagonista. Creo que es un problema de mentalidad", concluyó.

articles.title: How Brentford plan to develop the best young talent and break into the Premier League elite
articles.summary: Sky Sports' Uma Gurav goes behind the scenes at Brentford with the club's sporting director and technical director to uncover the secrets of their ongoing success...
articles.body:
But how do Brentford get to that next level? In their view, the answer could come via the academy.

In April, Brentford was awarded Category 1 status - the highest classification available - and their aim is to now transform into a system that is not only known for strong first-team recruitment but also one that produces academy graduates.

Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports News from under a brand-new dome being constructed to house the academy teams, sporting director Phil Giles and technical director Lee Dykes opened up about their roadmap to make Brentford one of the elites.

"Great with data? Great at recruitment? It's always nice to be all those things, obviously, but they are somewhat clichés at times," Giles, who runs the football side of Brentford, said. "I think we're a club who's just continually growing.

"This dome is part of it; this constant investment in the club, reinvestment of the benefits of being in the Premier League, growing the club not just from the playing point of view but also through the academy and in general, means that the club now looks hugely different to what it did 10 years ago. We want to keep getting better."

Dykes, who oversees recruitment and development, added: "The academy infrastructure is going to be so important. It's a lot simpler for me if we have the player in the building.

"We want to be that club that can build players through an academy into the next steps, which is U18s, B-team and then eventually first-team football. We'd love to do that."

That is easier said than done, however. Brentford will have to go up against the established academy systems of Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham, Fulham, Crystal Palace to attract the best young talent to London.

Having closed their academy while in the Championship in order to funnel funds towards getting promotion, Brentford have relied on youth development via their B-team and there have been some notable albeit limited success stories so far. The one that sticks out currently is Yehor Yarmoliuk - now a Bees centurion - who came from Ukraine as a teenager and has become an essential part of Keith Andrews' midfield.

They have high hopes for other talents, including the 19-year-old Belgian striker Kaye Furo - named PL2 Player of the Month in August - but one of the biggest challenges now is how to win in the battleground for the best prospects and answer the question: why should young talent choose Brentford?

Dykes said: "I think the academy thought-process has always been to compete in the marketplace, but also how do we become unique in the marketplace? (Being) caring and progressive has always been the angle that we've placed on the academy. Obviously, it's a lot more cost-effective for the club (too).

"(In Yarmoliuk) we have a player playing in our first team that's played over 100 times for Brentford in the Premier League that came through the B-team structure. We've proved we can do it to a certain extent. All of this investment, especially in this building, is geared towards producing that. That's the investment the club's made and I believe it's the right way."

'An asset to the Premier League' - How Brentford have defied the odds

After their first 10 games, Andrews' team are eighth on 14 points and going strong. As Giles explains, the club's ability to reach new heights every season is down to the phrase: "be an asset to the Premier League".

To get to where they are now, Brentford have not just had to survive but also overcome the challenge of regularly selling and replacing some of their best assets; none more so than in the summer of 2025 when long-term head coach Thomas Frank left for Tottenham, captain Christian Norgaard joined Arsenal, Bryan Mbeumo signed for Manchester United and Yoane Wissa went to Newcastle.

It was a pivotal summer that Giles plays down the impact of, but does admit could have seen them relegated had they got their decisions wrong.

"The summer Keith came in we sold some big players," he said. "Yeah, we might have got relegated. That might have happened. There's always a chance. There's a chance if you don't do that. It's about managing risk. It's particularly my job to get those decisions right.

"But show me a decision that isn't a risk. Show me a manager, head coach, who could come in and wouldn't be a risky appointment. We just felt that with Keith, we'd worked with him for a year, he'd been incredibly impressive, he's an incredibly impressive individual, great personality, great connection with the players, tactically knows his stuff, loved his willingness to become a set-piece coach, just to be at Brentford really. And he thoroughly earned his chance to have a go at it. We've thrown our support behind him, and it's gone okay I would say. So long may that continue."

'Timing is everything' - How Brentford snapped up Igor Thiago and Mamadou Sangare

A common perception of Brentford which the club are no doubt proud to own is their ability to unearth some of the world's best talent and turn them into Premier League stars.

Currently the most prominent one of these is last season's Golden Boot runner-up; Igor Thiago. Brentford signed him in 2024 from Club Brugge for a then club-record £30m to replace Ivan Toney but - as Dykes explained - he was on the radar long before.

"We tracked him for a lot of years, all the way back to when he was in Brazil," he says. "To be fair, he just did so well, wherever he was, he would move. We had to track him from there to there to there, and then eventually it was the right time. Timing in recruitment is everything.

"It would have been pointless for us to sign Igor any sooner than we did because we didn't have the spot in the team and the plan wouldn't have been true if we were sat in front of him saying, you're going to be our next number nine."

Brentford look like they may have found another star this summer too in Mamadou Sangare. He has made an instant impact and had barely started life in the Premier League before many began questioning why bigger clubs did not sign the him.

Dykes explained: "We were able to put our case forward of why he should come to Brentford because there were lots of other clubs speaking to him. I think we do well with that; our presentations are good.

"Obviously, he had a really good feeling with Keith at the time and he just felt that Brentford was the right step for him to go on to the next level and play Premier League football.

"We as a club just trust that we can deliver what we say to players and representatives and I think we've got a rich history of doing that, so I think players know a lot about Brentford.

"Once upon a time we used to have to tell people where Brentford was in England, location-wise, but now people know a hell of a lot about Brentford and that's obviously a testament to the good work of all the people that worked for the club in that time."

Europe on the horizon? Brentford remain coy on a top-six finish this term

Just as challenging as acquiring all these players has been hanging onto them. Giles joked 'I just don't pick the phone up' - even if 'it doesn't make you popular all the time', as a way of keeping hold of players.

There will no doubt be testing times again in January and next summer if the likes of Thiago, Sangare and forward Kevin Schade, whom the club want to sign a new contract, keep doing well.

Yet history tells us, no matter what happens next, the Bees will find a solution. One obvious next step would be to challenge for Europe, especially given they just missed out on goal-difference last season. Giles, however, remains grounded in the reality of the Premier League.

"We don't operate in isolation," he said. "There's 19 other teams all trying to be brilliant and trying to finish as high as possible, so all you can really do - and I know it's a bit of a cliché - is focus more on week-by-week, how are you going to prepare the team, that's Keith's job obviously, and just face the challenge in the short term. What will be, will be in the long term.

"We can just keep on following the mantra of being better and trying to improve, if we can keep doing that, and we keep achieving that, then inexorably, we should progress towards something, I just don't know what that something is yet."

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes tumbles as new No 1 is crowned: Sky Sports ranks the Premier League's top 25 players right now
articles.summary: Who are the best players in the Premier League right now? We asked the Sky Sports reporters and journalists to rank the contenders, collating a new top 25...
articles.body:
We asked our reporters and journalists to rank a longlist of 40 of the best players in the competition right now and took an average of their answers to produce the Sky Sports top 25.

The champions Arsenal the best represented, accounting for nine of the top 25. But which player takes top spot? And how do the rankings below compare to our last vote at the start of the season ?

Arsenal's conductor. The man who makes Mikel Arteta's attacking orchestra sing. When Odegaard finds his rhythm, so do the champions.

Chelsea aren't the same team when he's missing. Joao Pedro has the swagger, technical brilliance and imagination to unlock even the most stubborn defences. He leads the way for Chelsea when it comes to Premier League goals (20) and goal involvements (28) since the start of last season.

Anderson has developed into one of the Premier League's most complete midfield operators, combining the bite of a ball-winner with the brain of a playmaker and his stock is on the rise courtesy of his performances for Man City and England.

Anderson tops the charts for successful passes and duels won of midfielders in the Premier League this season.

Since the last top 25 was published in March he has improved by 12 places.

Football is supposed to be fun, remember. Cherki makes it. Man City's twinkle toes has turned his flamboyance into goal involvements this season, posting the second-best minutes per goal involvement (one every 81 mins) of players to have played a minimum of 500 minutes.

A gloriously unpredictable talent capable of turning a mundane passage of play into something spectacular.

The Rolls-Royce of Premier League centre-backs. Saliba makes defending look almost insultingly easy. A defender without an obvious weakness and it's been a surprise to see Arsenal cope so admirably without him this season.

Rogers has blossomed into one of the Premier League's most devastating attacking forces. His ability to glide past opponents with that deceptively explosive running style is frightening. And his rise five places up this ranking since March showcases his standing within the game.

A defensive monster. Gabriel has become the beating heart of Arsenal's extraordinary defensive machine, combining old-school aggression and an unmatched aerial presence in both boxes. Gabriel has scored the most goals by a Premier League defender since 2020/21 (21).

Every title-winning side needs a warrior. Arsenal have theirs.

The goalkeeper has helped redefine Arsenal's defensive output. Raya isn't merely a shot-stopper, he's an extra outfield player, a sweeper and a calming presence rolled into one who has kept more clean sheets since his debut (55) for Arsenal than any other goalkeeper in the Premier League.

But Rice remains just one short of the top player award, just like he did in March's rankings.

Rice is the engine, heartbeat and insurance policy of Arsenal. His ability to dominate midfield battles, cover enormous distances and influence games in both boxes makes him almost irreplaceable.

A goalscoring phenomenon who now tops this chart, moving up three places from March. In that period he has scored 14 Premier League goals - almost double that of the next player on that list.

Haaland takes the crown from Bruno Fernandes.

Just like Manchester United, Bruno Fernandes has tumbled. The United captain was sitting pretty at the summit of our Premier League top 25 rankings back in March. Eight months on? He's tumbled 10 places to 11th. Ouch.

It's a dramatic fall for a player who was previously regarded as the league's most influential performer. Fernandes remains a footballer of outrageous ability but United's struggles have made it increasingly difficult for their talisman to dominate matches.

And whose stolen his crown? A certain Norwegian goal machine.

Haaland has climbed three places from fourth to first. He's a cheat code. A footballing freak.

But the biggest shake-up comes further down the rankings.

A whopping 11 players have been given the boot out of the top 25. They are: Gianluigi Donnarumma, Jurrien Timber, Igor Thiago, Hugo Ekitike, Martin Zubimendi, Reece James, Bryan Mbeumo, Marc Guehi and Enzo Fernandez, with Bernardo Silva and Casemiro leaving the Premier League altogether.

Their replacements? Some serious star quality.

Cherki storms straight in at seventh, while Odegaard (10th), Isak (12th) and Palmer (13th) make eye-catching returns. Van Dijk (15th), Gross (17th), Konsa (19th), Doku (21st), Gibbs-White (22nd), Calafiori (23rd) and Alisson (25th) complete the new arrivals.

articles.title: 3 Things That Have Gone Wrong For Bruins During 3-Game Losing Streak
articles.summary: Boston has been in a slump, falling to Montreal, Minnesota and Los Angeles over the last week.
articles.body:
The Bruins opened the 2026-27 season with an impressive 8-1-1 mark at home. But that's fallen apart over the past week.

Boston is now on a three-game losing streak after falling 3-0 to the Kings on Tuesday night, with all three of those games being played at home. And in many ways, it was the toughest loss for the Bruins yet, with Los Angeles coming in with just five wins in its past 18 games.

It's been a rough stretch for the Bruins, needing to get back on track as they hit the road to face the Red Wings on Wednesday night.

Here are three things that have gone wrong for Boston during its three-game losing streak.

3 Things That Have Gone Wrong For Bruins During Losing Streak

In all three of Boston's losses over the past week, the team allowed the first goal. Digging an early hole has been a theme of all three games.

Against the Canadiens, Kirby Dach Goal found the back of the net just over two minutes into the game. Ryan Hartman struck first for the Wild in the second loss, and on Tuesday night, Mats Zuccarello gave the Kings an early advantage in the first period.

"I think we were all looking for one goal just to get us out of it, but the problem was that goal never came. ... We played more and more frustrated," Marco Sturm said after the loss, per CBS Sports . "The biggest thing for me is how we're going to get out of it. We have to go back to square one and remind ourselves what made us good."

Boston has been outscored 14-4 over its three-game skid, not generating nearly enough offense to keep up with its opponents. The Bruins had 13 games of at least three goals over their first 18 matchups, all of which were wins. When they were scoring, they were winning. Since then, they haven't had one.

The Kings had allowed two or more goals in every game this season prior to shutting out Boston, a concerning sign for Sturm's team. Facing strong goalies in Jacob Fowler and Jesper Wallstedt could have been an excuse for the Canadiens and Wild losses, but the loss to Los Angeles was more of an issue, as the Bruins had a season-low four high-danger chances against the Kings.

Dating back to Oct. 27, the Bruins are on a 3-for-30 slump on power-plays, including 0-for-2 against the Kings. There is little offense being converted right now.

"You can't just hope on the power play to score," Sturm said Tuesday. "In the 2nd period, we had like three 5-on-5 shots. That's not good enough. Still sometimes we go into the zone, and we're still looking to pass. Once in a while, you've got to get we call it a garbage goal, right? It's got to be a dirty goal."

Forwards Not Stepping Up, 'Mental' Frustrations

Through two periods against the Kings on Tuesday night, the Bruins only had one forward in their top nine with multiple shots on goal, which was Fraser Minten. In fact, three of those players didn't have a single shot, including Pavel Zacha, Casey Mittelstadt, and Marat Khusnutdinov.

In the absence of rookie James Hagans, who posted 12 points in his first 17 games, momentum has been harder to come by for the Bruins.

After falling to the Canadiens and Wild, the Bruins also fell to 1-5-0 this season when playing teams ranked ahead of them in the league standings. They've struggled to punch up, even if they're clearly in the playoff race themselves.

Boston did out-shoot Los Angeles 29-22, but Sturm pointed to mental frustrations as one potential reason for the slump.

"I think the mental part of the game, we're just probably not the strongest right now and you could tell," Sturm said on Tuesday night. "We were all looking for one goal just to get us out of it tonight, but the problem was that goal never came, so that's why we kind of almost got stuck today. And they played really smart, didn't do much, and we got a little bit more and more frustrated and made some mental mistakes, and all of a sudden you lose the game. So it was a little frustrating today, for sure."

articles.title: From Dunfermline to Dubai - James McPake on new life in Middle East
articles.summary: James McPake has left Scottish football behind for the time being, plying his trade in coaching in Dubai.
articles.body:
James McPake may not have given up on football management but the former Dundee and Dunfermline Athletic boss is discovering there is life beyond the dugout.

Four months after moving to Dubai with his family, the 41-year-old has settled into a new role working in schools to develop young players.

It is a considerable change from the pressures of Scottish football but one that McPake and his family had been contemplating for more than a year.

His wife Dawn, a teacher, secured a position in Dubai before McPake landed his own opportunity, one that has opened up a different world of opportunities, including working alongside some recognisable names in football.

"It's certainly a bit different from back home but we're enjoying it," he says. "There is obviously a big demand for British curriculum teachers, so Dawn managed to get a position and I've been pretty fortunate to land here."

The timing of the family's move has inevitably attracted attention, given the wider tensions in the Middle East and concerns about security in the region.

However, McPake insists their experience of living in Dubai has been very different from some of the headlines.

"You don't hear a lot about it and you don't see anything. It is very much business as usual," he explains. "It's as busy as when we've come here on holiday. It's just like being anywhere else.

"The girls are enjoying it. They feel safe, they enjoy school and they can go out and play at night. We've had no issues that I've seen."

McPake's decision to head overseas has also provided an opportunity to step away from the demands of management and concentrate on developing players.

His responsibilities include overseeing under-16 and under-19 programmes at an impressive set-up, with school timetables adapted to accommodate training and facilities including strength and conditioning rooms, pools and pitches.

"The programme is relatively new but it's similar to the way you would look at an SFA performance school," he says. "The facilities are fantastic. It's difficult not to make a difference when you have facilities like these."

Former Real Madrid and Wales star Gareth Bale recently spent time at the school, answering questions from senior pupils during an hour-long session. And ex- England midfielder Jonjo Shelvey is also working full-time with McPake.

"For the kids, it was a fantastic experience," the former Livingston and Hibernian defender says.

"Gareth sat with myself and the head director of sport and answered question after question. Afterwards, we saw him out on the pitch with some of the younger kids, and Jonjo was on one of our other pitches.

"It's brilliant for the youngsters to have that sort of access to people who have played at the highest level."

McPake's departure from Scotland came at a time when opportunities were becoming increasingly difficult to secure. He admits that was a consideration in the move but not the driving force behind the family's decision.

There remains an obvious desire to return to the dugout but for now he is happy to embrace a different challenge.

"We've always wanted to give this a go, particularly for the girls. We wanted them to have an experience of a different society and culture and broaden their eyes to the world while they were still young," he says.

"The lack of opportunities in Scotland didn't make the decision for us but it certainly didn't cause us any hesitation when we were looking at coming out here.

"We've now been here for a few months, we're settled and we're used to life out here. It's been excellent and better than we imagined."

'No bitterness towards Dundee and Dunfermline'

Although he is now thousands of miles away, McPake continues to follow Scottish football closely, particularly the fortunes of two clubs where he managed.

Dundee, where he was in charge between 2019 and 2022, have impressed him under Steven Pressley. And he also retains an affection for Dunfermline, where he won the League 1 title.

There is particular pride in watching youngsters he helped introduce to senior football begin to make their mark at a higher level.

"Luke Graham getting his first start for Scotland the other night was fantastic. He's a great kid and, even when he was really young and training with us at Dundee, you could see he was going to be the next one," says McPake, who played once for Northern Ireland.

McPake also keeps an eye on the progress of Dunfermline's Tod brothers, Andrew and Jon, who have both progressed through the Scotland international age groups.

There is also no lingering resentment towards either Dundee or Dunfermline, despite the manner in which his managerial spells ended.

McPake acknowledges that losing a job hurts but insists the affection he has for both clubs remains.

"At Dundee, it was excellent," he adds. "I have no bitterness towards them and Dunfermline is the same. We felt we weren't quite backed there.

"Should we have done better? Yes. But we won a very strong League 1 and then they just didn't push on in the Championship."

articles.title: Signs of life — Charlie’s Film Room Week 11
articles.summary: Something to build on.
articles.body:
After starting the season 6-1, Northwestern has lost its last three games. This was the toughest stretch of the season for sure, but with how the beginning part of the year played out for the 'Cats and for teams like Oregon and Ohio State, there was a real path to make the College Football Playoff. At 6-2 after the Oregon loss, if Northwestern had won out, it still could have been reality. However, not having Aidan Chiles the last two games has been detrimental. That's not to say that Nicco Marchiol has been playing poorly — he's been serviceable and hasn't made mistakes. The problem lies in that there seems to be a different level of trust in Chiles that can be seen in the play calling with Marchiol under center. This film review is going to be shorter for sure, but I'm focusing on what was the best part from Northwestern's offensive performance in Columbus.

Against Iowa, I can't remember a time where Marchiol tried to extend the field through the air. Against Ohio State, it was few and far between for the most part, but there were a few plays (especially on the final drive) that looked more like the Northwestern offense had with Chiles.

On the first play, Marchiol steps up in the pocket and then starts to take off. If this were the Iowa game, Marchiol would have likely kept it himself. Instead, he lobs it over the head of the trailing defender to Luke Dehnicke who cut upfield to get open after his initial draft route. The second play is a quick hitter out of the gun, with Marchiol faking the handoff to Gavin Sawchuk before throwing a laser to Alex Honig up the seam. Honig gained 37 on the play for the 'Cats with some YAC.

On the third play, Ohio State is in man, and Marchiol works through his progressions before finding Griffin Wilde across the middle on the dig route. This was the first play of Northwestern's final drive as the Wildcats were down 28-13, so it was an obvious passing situation. However, it was the most comfortable Marchiol looked throwing the football and stretching the field this season (apart from a few earlier throws in this game). In a game where Wilde wasn't targeted until late in the fourth quarter, Marchiol started to develop a stronger rapport on this drive. On the fourth play, he trusts Wilde and waits for him to stop at the top of his curl route before timing his throw so only Wilde could get it.

On the fifth play, the switch concept that Wilde and Dehnicke run on the right side allows for Dehnicke to get a step on his defender with his cut upfield, and then Marchiol hits him in stride down the sideline for a 41-yard gain: the longest play for the 'Cats this season with No. 4 under center. On the last play in this cutup, Ohio State only rushes three and has the rest of the defense drop back to the end zone. Marchiol throws it up for Dehnicke on the right sideline of the end zone, and the tight end makes a play to score a touchdown. Even though it was a risky throw (and necessary in the situation), seeing the ball pushed downfield on this last drive in a two-minute drill with Marchiol at quarterback looked like it could be a blueprint for Northwestern in its remaining games this season — especially if Chiles remains out.

articles.title: Rees-Zammit: From beating All Blacks to meeting Man Utd heroes
articles.summary: Louis Rees-Zammit has had a week to remember having helped Wales to a historic win over New Zealand and meeting his Manchester United heroes.
articles.body:
Louis Rees-Zammit has had some memorable weeks, but might be hard-pressed to remember a better one having helped Wales to a historic victory over New Zealand and coming face-to-face with his Manchester United heroes.

The 25-year-old wing scored in Wales' 35-28 victory which ended a 73-year losing streak against the mighty All Blacks.

"We couldn't quite believe what we did, but at the same time we were just so excited and happy that we could put a performance on that the nation could be proud," Rees-Zammit said.

Three days later, he was at Cardiff City Stadium to watch Wales play Portgual in the Nations League and was given a personal meeting with Bruno Fernandes and Diogo Dalot.

"As a Man Utd fan I was a bit starstruck to be honest. I was shaking a little bit when I was shaking their hands. It was crazy and to be able to meet them in person was really special," he said.

It seems hard to believe that someone of Rees-Zammit's profile would get starstruck, but such is the humility of the player.

His return to form, and to the wing, has been a breath of fresh air to Welsh rugby, who sorely missed their poster boy when he left to pursue a career in American football in 2024.

"Whenever I get an opportunity to put on the red shirt it's always a dream come true," said the Bristol player.

"Those two years [in the NFL] made me realise how much I missed playing rugby and representing my country and obviously moments like Saturday are there to celebrate, with family, friends and the nation.

"That was the best atmosphere I have ever been a part of. The fans were unbelievable.

"They play a massive part in the way we play and how much momentum we can build in the game. The 55,000 that were there made such a noise.

"Every turnover, every hold up over the line, they really cheered us on to keep doing it over and over again."

Wales had failed to beat New Zealand in 34 previous attempts and despite some close calls over the years, few gave them any hope last Saturday.

But the players certainly did not have the mindset.

Rees-Zammit admits they knew victory was in their sights as soon as half-time, when the sides went in level at 21-21.

"A lot of the boys were talking about how we had the opportunity to beat the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years. On top of that, when Dewi [Lake, Wales captain] brought us in, it just gave us that extra energy and belief that we could do it.

"It was about how relentless we could be, could we start fast again and really put them under pressure and I think we did that.

"Obviously going out in the second half and starting fast, scoring two tries and being 14 points up, was absolutely huge. Sam Costelow off the tee as well, not missing at all."

Wales must now prove against Australia on Saturday that they are capable of claiming another major scalp, especially with 2027 being a World Cup year.

The Wallabies arrive in Cardiff after four straight defeats, but showed their potential in the summer by beating world champions South Africa.

Rees-Zammit says Wales must continue up their upward trajectory.

"In the Six Nations we started to build nicely, from start to finish it was on the up. Over the summer we beat Fiji and then went to Argentina and South Africa and lost, but those performances were not us," he said.

"This autumn we've really started to build some momentum in training weeks and come Saturdays we're full of confidence and belief.

"To be able to beat the All Blacks is obviously unbelievably special, but it's about backing it up.

"Reviewing last weekend's game, there are a lot of areas where we can still improve."
